337	**[Section 5 --- Incident Response and Severity Classification]{.underline}**
338	
339	**[5.1 Severity Level Definitions]{.underline}**
340	
341	The vendor shall classify all incidents using the following **four-tier severity classification system**. The vendor agreement must adopt this four-tier model in its entirety. Vendor agreements proposing fewer than four severity levels, or severity level definitions that are inconsistent with the definitions set forth below, shall be modified to conform to this standard. Meridian shall retain the right to reclassify any incident to a higher severity level if, in Meridian\'s reasonable judgment, the vendor\'s initial classification does not accurately reflect the impact of the incident.
342	
343	**Severity 1 (S1) --- Critical:** Complete system unavailability, or any incident involving actual or suspected compromise of the integrity, confidentiality, or availability of Protected Health Information (\"PHI\"). Severity 1 incidents include, without limitation: total platform outage affecting all or substantially all users; confirmed or suspected data breach involving unauthorized access to, acquisition of, or disclosure of PHI; ransomware attack or other malicious intrusion affecting systems that process, store, or transmit PHI; data corruption affecting clinical records, patient histories, or medication orders; and failure of disaster recovery or failover systems during a primary system outage. Any incident involving the actual or suspected compromise of PHI shall be classified as Severity 1 regardless of the number of users or records affected.
344	
345	**Severity 2 (S2) --- High:** Significant system degradation that materially impairs patient care workflows, including but not limited to: inability to access patient records in emergency, inpatient, or surgical settings; failure or degradation of clinical decision support alerts or warnings; degradation affecting the ordering, dispensing, or administration of medications; failure of laboratory results delivery to ordering providers; and patient portal unavailability lasting more than thirty (30) minutes during business hours. An incident affecting more than ten percent (10%) of clinical users at any Meridian facility shall presumptively be classified as Severity 2 or higher, subject to reclassification to Severity 1 if the criteria in the preceding paragraph are met.
346	
347	**Severity 3 (S3) --- Medium:** System degradation that materially impairs administrative or non-clinical workflows but does not directly impact patient care or the integrity of PHI. Examples include: billing system processing delays, reporting module errors or slowness, patient portal aesthetic or minor functional issues not affecting clinical data access, and HR or payroll system degradation.
348	
349	**Severity 4 (S4) --- Low:** Cosmetic issues, minor defects, or requests for information that do not materially impair any clinical, administrative, or business workflow. Examples include: user interface formatting or display issues, non-critical feature requests, minor documentation errors, and informational inquiries.
350	
351	**[5.2 Response Time Requirements]{.underline}**
352	
353	The vendor shall acknowledge and begin active work on each incident within the following timeframes, measured from the earlier of: (i) the time Meridian reports the incident to the vendor through any designated communication channel, or (ii) the time the vendor\'s monitoring systems detect the incident:
354	
355	  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
356	  **Severity Level**                  **Maximum Response Time**
357	  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
358	  **S1 --- Critical**                 **15 minutes**
359	
360	  **S2 --- High**                     **1 hour**
361	
362	  **S3 --- Medium**                   **4 hours**
363	
364	  **S4 --- Low**                      **1 business day**
365	  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
366	
367	\"Response\" means that a qualified technical resource has been assigned to the incident, has acknowledged receipt of the incident report, and has begun active diagnostic or remediation work. Automated acknowledgment messages, ticket creation confirmations, and auto-generated status notifications do not constitute a \"response\" for purposes of these Standards. The assigned resource must possess the technical qualifications and system access necessary to diagnose and remediate the incident without further escalation or handoff.
368	
369	**[5.3 Resolution Time Requirements]{.underline}**
370	
371	The vendor shall resolve each incident --- meaning restore the affected service to full functionality or implement a workaround that is acceptable to Meridian in Meridian\'s reasonable judgment --- within the following timeframes:
372	
373	  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
374	  **Severity Level**                  **Maximum Resolution Time**
375	  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
376	  **S1 --- Critical**                 **4 hours**
377	
378	  **S2 --- High**                     **12 hours**
379	
380	  **S3 --- Medium**                   **3 business days**
381	
382	  **S4 --- Low**                      **10 business days**
383	  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
384	
385	Resolution times are measured from the same starting point as response times (the earlier of Meridian\'s report or the vendor\'s detection). A workaround shall be deemed \"acceptable to Meridian\" only if it restores the essential functionality affected by the incident without materially degrading performance, introducing additional risk, or requiring Meridian personnel to perform manual processes that are ordinarily automated.
386	
387	**[5.4 Binding Nature of Response and Resolution Commitments]{.underline}**
388	
389	**All response and resolution times set forth in Sections 5.2 and 5.3 are binding SLA commitments, not aspirational targets, commercially reasonable efforts goals, or best-efforts obligations.** The vendor agreement shall expressly state that these commitments are binding obligations. The vendor agreement shall not characterize these commitments as \"targets,\" \"goals,\" \"objectives,\" \"commercially reasonable efforts,\" or \"best efforts.\" Any proposed vendor agreement using such language with respect to incident response or resolution times shall be returned to the vendor for revision.
390	
391	Failure to meet the response time or resolution time for a Severity 1 (S1) or Severity 2 (S2) incident shall trigger the following consequences:
392	
393	> \(a\) **Immediate Escalation.** The incident shall be immediately escalated to the vendor\'s senior management, including at minimum a Vice President-level executive, who shall assume direct oversight of the incident until resolution.
394	>
395	> \(b\) **Additional Service Credits.** The vendor shall issue an additional service credit equal to five percent (5%) of the monthly fee for each hour (or fraction thereof) by which the response or resolution exceeds the applicable commitment set forth in Sections 5.2 and 5.3. These additional service credits are in addition to, and not in lieu of, the uptime-based service credits specified in Section 4.1.
396	>
397	> \(c\) **Mandatory Root Cause Analysis.** The vendor shall deliver a written root cause analysis to Meridian\'s CISO and VP of IT Procurement within forty-eight (48) hours of the resolution of the incident, detailing the cause of the response or resolution delay, corrective actions taken, and preventive measures to be implemented.
398	
399	Failure to meet response or resolution times for Severity 3 (S3) and Severity 4 (S4) incidents shall trigger escalation and reporting obligations but shall not trigger additional service credits unless the failure is part of a pattern of non-compliance, defined as three (3) or more S3/S4 response or resolution failures within a single calendar quarter.
400	
401	**[5.5 Incident Reporting and Communication]{.underline}**
402	
403	For Severity 1 (S1) and Severity 2 (S2) incidents, the vendor shall provide real-time status updates to Meridian\'s designated incident contacts, including at minimum the CISO, Dr. Priya Nandakumar, and the VP of IT Procurement, Marcus Ellison, at intervals of no greater than **thirty (30) minutes** until the incident is resolved. Status updates shall include the current status of the incident, diagnostic findings, actions being taken, estimated time to resolution, and the identity of the technical resources assigned to the incident.
404	
405	For Severity 3 (S3) incidents, the vendor shall provide status updates to the designated contacts every four (4) hours during Meridian\'s business hours (7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Eastern Time, Monday through Friday) until the incident is resolved.
406	
407	The vendor shall maintain a dedicated incident communication channel, staffed by qualified technical personnel, available **24 hours per day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year** for Severity 1 and Severity 2 incidents. The dedicated channel shall include, at minimum, a telephone hotline and a monitored email address. The vendor shall deliver a final **post-incident report (\"PIR\")** for all S1 and S2 incidents within **five (5) business days** of resolution. The PIR shall include a complete root cause analysis, a detailed timeline of events from detection through resolution, a description of corrective actions taken, and a plan for preventive measures to avoid recurrence.

409	**[Section 6 --- Data Security Requirements]{.underline}**
410	
411	**[6.1 Regulatory Compliance]{.underline}**
412	
413	The vendor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations governing the privacy and security of health information, including without limitation:
414	
415	> \(a\) the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (\"HIPAA\"), including the Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 160 and Subparts A and E of Part 164), the Security Rule (45 CFR Part 160 and Subparts A and C of Part 164), and the Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR §§ 164.400--414);
416	>
417	> \(b\) the **Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act of 2009 (\"HITECH Act\"), codified at 42 U.S.C. § 17931 et seq.**, including all regulations promulgated thereunder, specifically including the provisions regarding: (i) the application of the HIPAA Security Rule to business associates (42 U.S.C. § 17931); (ii) notification requirements in the case of breach (42 U.S.C. § 17932); (iii) limitations on the sale of PHI (42 U.S.C. § 17935(d)); (iv) enhanced penalties for willful neglect (42 U.S.C. § 17939); and (v) the extension of enforcement authority to state attorneys general (42 U.S.C. § 17939(d)); and
418	>
419	> \(c\) applicable state privacy and breach notification laws, including without limitation the North Carolina Identity Theft Protection Act, the South Carolina Insurance Data Security Act, and the Georgia Personal Identity Protection Act.
420	
421	Any Business Associate Agreement (\"BAA\") entered into between Meridian and the vendor **shall expressly incorporate by reference both HIPAA and the HITECH Act**, including the HITECH Act\'s specific codification at 42 U.S.C. § 17931 et seq. and all amendments and successor regulations. The vendor shall acknowledge in the BAA that it is a \"business associate\" as defined under both HIPAA (45 CFR § 160.103) and the HITECH Act, and that it is directly subject to the HITECH Act\'s enforcement provisions, breach notification requirements, enhanced penalty framework, and the obligations extended to business associates by the Omnibus Rule (78 Fed. Reg. 5566 (Jan. 25, 2013)). A BAA that references only HIPAA without express incorporation of the HITECH Act shall not satisfy this requirement.
422	
423	**[6.2 Encryption Standards]{.underline}**
424	
425	The vendor shall implement and maintain encryption standards consistent with or exceeding the following minimum requirements:
426	
427	> \(a\) **Data at Rest.** All Customer Data, including PHI, stored on any system, device, storage medium, or backup media controlled by the vendor or its subcontractors shall be encrypted using the **Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) with a key length of 256 bits (AES-256)**, or a successor encryption standard approved in writing by Meridian\'s CISO. Encryption shall apply to all storage tiers, including primary storage, secondary storage, archival storage, and disaster recovery copies.
428	>
429	> \(b\) **Data in Transit.** All Customer Data transmitted over any network, including the vendor\'s internal networks, public internet, private interconnections, and connections between data centers, shall be encrypted using **Transport Layer Security (TLS) version 1.2 or higher**. The vendor shall disable all legacy encryption protocols, including but not limited to SSL (all versions), TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1, on all systems and endpoints used to process, transmit, or store Meridian\'s Customer Data.
430	>
431	> \(c\) **Encryption Key Management.** The vendor shall maintain encryption key management practices consistent with NIST Special Publication 800-57 (Recommendation for Key Management). Encryption keys shall be rotated at least annually, and more frequently if warranted by a security incident or key compromise. The vendor shall maintain separation of duties between encryption key custodians and system administrators.
432	
433	The vendor agreement **shall not use vague or undefined encryption language such as \"industry-standard encryption,\" \"commercially reasonable encryption,\" or \"appropriate encryption methods.\"** The specific encryption algorithms and minimum key lengths set forth in this Section 6.2 shall be expressly stated in the vendor agreement and any applicable exhibits or security addenda.
434	
435	**[6.3 Security Certifications and Assessments]{.underline}**
436	
437	The vendor shall obtain and maintain the following security certifications and shall provide evidence of current certification to Meridian upon request and no less than annually:
438	
439	> \(a\) **SOC 2 Type II Report.** The vendor shall maintain a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy, issued by an independent third-party auditor within the preceding twelve (12) months. The report shall cover all systems, data centers, and processes used in connection with the services provided to Meridian.
440	>
441	> \(b\) **HITRUST Common Security Framework (CSF) Certification.** The vendor shall maintain a validated HITRUST CSF assessment and certification, current as of the effective date of the vendor agreement and maintained throughout the term. The HITRUST CSF certification shall cover the vendor\'s healthcare-related systems, processes, and controls.
442	
443	In addition to the foregoing certifications, the vendor shall:
444	
445	> \(c\) **Annual Third-Party Penetration Testing.** The vendor shall conduct annual third-party penetration testing of all systems used to process, store, or transmit Meridian\'s Customer Data, including PHI. The penetration test shall be performed by a qualified, independent third-party security firm that is not affiliated with the vendor. The vendor shall provide Meridian with a copy of the penetration testing report, including all findings, risk ratings, and remediation plans, **within thirty (30) days of completion** of each test.
446	>
447	> \(d\) **Quarterly Vulnerability Scanning.** The vendor shall conduct internal and external vulnerability scans no less than quarterly and provide summary results, including remediation status for identified vulnerabilities, to Meridian upon request.
448	
449	**[6.4 Administrative, Technical, and Physical Safeguards]{.underline}**
450	
451	The vendor shall implement and maintain administrative, technical, and physical safeguards that meet or exceed the standards set forth in the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR §§ 164.308, 164.310, 164.312) and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (current version). The vendor agreement **shall specify the vendor\'s safeguard obligations with particularity and shall not rely on vague language such as \"commercially reasonable safeguards,\" \"appropriate safeguards,\" or \"industry-standard security measures\"** without further definition or specificity.
452	
453	At minimum, the vendor\'s safeguard obligations shall include: multi-factor authentication (\"MFA\") for all administrative, privileged, and remote access; role-based access controls with least-privilege principles; comprehensive audit logging with a minimum retention period of twelve (12) months; intrusion detection and prevention systems (\"IDS/IPS\"); endpoint detection and response (\"EDR\") on all systems processing Customer Data; network segmentation isolating systems that process PHI; documented incident response plans tested at least annually through tabletop or simulation exercises; and documented disaster recovery and business continuity plans tested at least annually with results reported to Meridian.
454	
455	**[6.5 De-Identified Data]{.underline}**
456	
457	If the vendor seeks to use Customer Data in de-identified form, as defined in 45 CFR § 164.514(a) and subject to the requirements of 45 CFR § 164.514(b) (safe harbor method) or 45 CFR § 164.514(c) (expert determination method), such use shall be subject to the following requirements:
458	
459	> \(a\) De-identified data may be used **only for purposes that directly benefit Meridian**, such as analytics, reporting, benchmarking, and performance dashboards provided to Meridian in connection with the contracted services.
460	>
461	> \(b\) The vendor shall **not** use de-identified data for the vendor\'s own product development, product improvement, service enhancement, benchmarking reports for the vendor\'s benefit or commercial use, or sale or license to third parties, without Meridian\'s prior written consent, which may be withheld or conditioned in Meridian\'s sole discretion.
462	>
463	> \(c\) Meridian shall have the right to **opt out** of any de-identified data use program at any time upon written notice to the vendor, and the vendor shall cease such use within thirty (30) days of receiving the opt-out notice.
464	>
465	> \(d\) The vendor shall maintain complete documentation of its de-identification methodology, including the method employed (safe harbor or expert determination), and shall make such documentation available to Meridian for review upon request.
466	
467	**[6.6 Cyber Liability Insurance]{.underline}**
468	
469	The vendor shall obtain and maintain throughout the term of the vendor agreement a cyber liability insurance policy (also known as technology errors and omissions / cyber liability insurance) with coverage limits of not less than **ten million dollars (\$10,000,000) per occurrence and in the aggregate**.
470	
471	The policy shall provide coverage for, at minimum:
472	
473	> \(a\) data breach response costs, including notification costs, credit monitoring, identity theft remediation, call center services, and forensic investigation;
474	>
475	> \(b\) regulatory defense costs and penalties, including fines and assessments imposed by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, state attorneys general, and other regulatory authorities;
476	>
477	> \(c\) business interruption losses, including Meridian\'s lost revenue and extra expense arising from vendor service disruptions;
478	>
479	> \(d\) network security liability, including claims arising from unauthorized access, denial-of-service attacks, and transmission of malicious code; and
480	>
481	> \(e\) media liability, including claims arising from content-related liabilities.
482	
483	The vendor shall name Meridian as an additional insured under the policy where permissible under the policy terms. The vendor shall provide Meridian with a certificate of insurance evidencing the required coverage upon execution of the vendor agreement, upon each policy renewal, and upon Meridian\'s request. The vendor shall provide Meridian with not less than **thirty (30) days\' prior written notice** of any cancellation, non-renewal, or material reduction in coverage.
484	
485	**[Section 7 --- Data Ownership, Portability, and Transition Assistance]{.underline}**
486	
487	**[7.1 Ownership of Customer Data]{.underline}**
488	
489	**Meridian shall retain sole and exclusive ownership of all Customer Data at all times.** No provision of the vendor agreement shall be construed to transfer, assign, or convey to the vendor any ownership interest in Customer Data. \"Customer Data\" means all data, information, records, and materials provided by or on behalf of Meridian to the vendor, or generated, collected, processed, or derived by the vendor in connection with the services, including without limitation all PHI, patient records, clinical data, diagnostic data, laboratory results, medication records, financial data, administrative data, employee data, metadata, system configuration data, and usage analytics.
490	
491	The vendor agreement shall grant the vendor **no license to Customer Data beyond what is strictly necessary to perform the contracted services** during the term of the agreement. Specifically, the vendor agreement shall **not** grant the vendor the right to:
492	
493	> \(a\) modify Customer Data or create derivative works from Customer Data, except as necessary to perform the contracted services and expressly authorized in writing by Meridian;
494	>
495	> \(b\) use Customer Data for the vendor\'s own product improvement, product development, feature enhancement, algorithm training, or machine learning purposes;
496	>
497	> \(c\) use Customer Data for analytics, benchmarking, competitive intelligence, or other purposes unrelated to the direct provision of the contracted services to Meridian; or
498	>
499	> \(d\) sublicense, distribute, sell, or otherwise make Customer Data available to any third party, except as expressly authorized in writing by Meridian.
500	
501	Upon termination or expiration of the vendor agreement for any reason, the vendor\'s limited license to access and use Customer Data shall immediately and automatically terminate, subject only to the Data Retrieval Period specified in Section 7.2 of these Standards. The vendor shall not retain any copies of Customer Data following the expiration of the Data Retrieval Period, except as required by applicable law or regulation, and any retained copies shall continue to be subject to the confidentiality and security obligations of the vendor agreement and BAA.
502	
503	**[7.2 Post-Termination Data Retrieval]{.underline}**
504	
505	Upon termination or expiration of the vendor agreement for any reason, whether by Meridian, by the vendor, or by operation of the agreement\'s terms, the vendor shall make all Customer Data available for retrieval by Meridian for a minimum period of **ninety (90) days** following the effective date of termination or expiration (the \"Data Retrieval Period\").
506	
507	During the Data Retrieval Period, the vendor shall:
508	
509	> \(a\) maintain all Customer Data in a secure, accessible state consistent with the security requirements of the vendor agreement and these Standards, including all encryption, access control, and monitoring obligations;
510	>
511	> \(b\) provide Customer Data to Meridian in **Meridian\'s specified format**, which at minimum shall include: **(i) HL7 FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) format** for all clinical data, patient records, and health information, and **(ii) CSV (Comma-Separated Values) format** for all administrative, financial, and non-clinical data. If Meridian specifies additional or alternative formats, the vendor shall accommodate such requests at no additional charge;
512	>
513	> \(c\) not charge Meridian any additional fees for data export or retrieval during the Data Retrieval Period beyond the fees already specified in the vendor agreement as of the date of termination or expiration;
514	>
515	> \(d\) cooperate fully with Meridian and any successor vendor designated by Meridian to facilitate complete, accurate, and timely data transfer, including providing technical support, data mapping assistance, and schema documentation; and
516	>
517	> \(e\) provide Meridian with written confirmation that the data export is complete and that all Customer Data has been made available for retrieval.
518	
519	Upon expiration of the Data Retrieval Period, and upon written confirmation from Meridian that data retrieval is complete, the vendor shall securely destroy all copies of Customer Data, including backups, archives, and disaster recovery copies, in accordance with NIST Special Publication 800-88 (Guidelines for Media Sanitization) and shall provide Meridian with a written certification of destruction signed by an authorized officer of the vendor within fifteen (15) days of completion of destruction.
520	
521	**[7.3 Transition Assistance]{.underline}**
522	
523	The vendor agreement shall include a detailed **Transition Assistance Plan** setting forth the vendor\'s obligations to assist Meridian in migrating to a successor vendor or to an in-house system. The Transition Assistance Plan shall be developed collaboratively by the parties during contract negotiation and documented as an exhibit to the vendor agreement.
524	
525	Transition assistance requirements include:
526	
527	> \(a\) **Duration.** The vendor shall provide transition assistance for a period of up to **twelve (12) months** following the effective date of termination or expiration, at rates pre-agreed in the vendor agreement.
528	>
529	> \(b\) **Plan Contents.** The Transition Assistance Plan shall identify: (i) dedicated vendor personnel assigned to the transition, including named individuals and their roles; (ii) a timeline and milestones for data migration, system cutover, and knowledge transfer; (iii) comprehensive data mapping and schema documentation, including data dictionaries, entity-relationship diagrams, and API specifications; (iv) API access and integration support, including the provision of documented APIs for data extraction and system integration; and (v) parallel operations support during the transition period, during which the vendor shall maintain the existing service at agreed service levels while the migration is underway.
530	>
531	> \(c\) **No Conditioning on Fees.** The vendor shall not condition the provision of transition assistance on the payment of any termination fee, early termination penalty, or outstanding disputed amount.
532	>
533	> \(d\) **Transition Assistance Fees.** Transition assistance fees shall be specified in the vendor agreement at the time of execution and shall not exceed the vendor\'s then-current published professional services rates or, if no published rates exist, rates consistent with the professional services rates in the original agreement, adjusted for inflation not to exceed three percent (3%) per annum.
534	
535	**[Section 8 --- Subcontractor Requirements]{.underline}**
536	
537	**[8.1 Prior Written Consent]{.underline}**
538	
539	The vendor shall not engage or permit any subcontractor, sub-processor, or third-party service provider to access, process, store, or transmit Meridian\'s Customer Data, including PHI, without Meridian\'s **prior written consent**. This requirement applies regardless of the subcontractor\'s role, the nature of the services to be subcontracted, or the volume of Customer Data involved.
540	
541	The vendor shall submit a subcontractor approval request to Meridian\'s VP of IT Procurement and CISO no less than **thirty (30) days** before the proposed engagement date. The approval request shall include, at minimum:
542	
543	> \(a\) the subcontractor\'s full legal name, principal place of business, and physical location(s) where services will be performed;
544	>
545	> \(b\) a detailed description of the nature and scope of Customer Data the subcontractor will access, process, store, or transmit;
546	>
547	> \(c\) the subcontractor\'s relevant security certifications, including SOC 2 Type II reports, HITRUST CSF certification status, and results of recent penetration testing; and
548	>
549	> \(d\) a copy of the proposed subcontract or data processing agreement between the vendor and the subcontractor.
550	
551	**Meridian shall have the right to object** to any proposed subcontractor within fifteen (15) days of receiving a complete approval request. If Meridian objects, the vendor shall not engage the proposed subcontractor for any work involving Meridian\'s Customer Data. The vendor shall propose an alternative subcontractor or perform the services directly. The vendor\'s failure to obtain Meridian\'s prior written consent before engaging a subcontractor shall constitute a material breach of the vendor agreement.
552	
553	**[8.2 Flow-Down Obligations]{.underline}**
554	
555	The vendor shall ensure that all approved subcontractors are bound by written agreements that impose obligations **at least as protective** of Meridian\'s interests as those contained in the vendor agreement, including without limitation:
556	
557	> \(a\) the same security and privacy obligations, including full HIPAA and HITECH Act compliance and the execution of a subcontractor BAA;
558	>
559	> \(b\) the same service level commitments, including uptime, incident response, and resolution time requirements;
560	>
561	> \(c\) the same audit rights, permitting both the vendor and Meridian to audit the subcontractor\'s compliance;
562	>
563	> \(d\) the same data handling, ownership, portability, and destruction obligations; and
564	>
565	> \(e\) the same confidentiality obligations.
566	
567	The vendor shall remain fully responsible and liable for the acts and omissions of all subcontractors as if such acts and omissions were the vendor\'s own. The vendor shall make subcontractor agreements available to Meridian for review upon request and shall promptly notify Meridian of any breach or non-compliance by a subcontractor.
568	
569	**[8.3 Data Hosting Location Restrictions]{.underline}**
570	
571	Customer Data, including all PHI, shall be hosted, processed, and stored only in data center locations **specifically approved in writing by Meridian** and identified by city and state (or city and country, if applicable) in the vendor agreement. The vendor agreement shall include a schedule or exhibit listing all approved data center locations.
572	
573	The vendor shall not migrate, replicate, or transfer Customer Data to any data center location not listed in the vendor agreement without Meridian\'s prior written consent. The vendor shall provide Meridian with no less than **ninety (90) days\' prior written notice** of any proposed change in data hosting location and shall obtain Meridian\'s written consent before effecting any such change. Meridian may withhold consent in its sole discretion.
574	
575	Customer Data shall at all times remain within the continental United States. No Customer Data shall be hosted, processed, stored, or accessed from any location outside the continental United States without Meridian\'s prior written consent, which may be withheld in Meridian\'s sole discretion.
576	
577	**[Section 9 --- Limitation of Liability]{.underline}**
578	
579	**[9.1 Liability Cap]{.underline}**
580	
581	The vendor agreement shall include a limitation of liability provision, provided that the vendor\'s total aggregate liability cap shall be no less than **twenty-four (24) months of total fees** payable under the agreement. \"Total fees\" for purposes of calculating the liability cap shall include all subscription fees, implementation fees, professional services fees, customization fees, support and maintenance fees, and any other fees payable under the agreement, whether paid on a recurring or one-time basis.
582	
583	For agreements involving a combination of recurring and one-time fees, the liability cap shall be calculated by annualizing all fees over the initial term and multiplying by two (2). For example, for an agreement with annual subscription fees of \$6.84 million and one-time implementation fees of \$4.5 million over a five-year term:
584	
585	> Total annual fees = \$6.84M + (\$4.5M ÷ 5 years) = \$6.84M + \$0.9M = \$7.74M per year
586	>
587	> Minimum 24-month liability cap = \$7.74M × 2 = **\$15.48 million**
588	
589	Vendor agreements proposing a liability cap below the 24-month total fees minimum, or proposing a cap calculated solely on subscription fees to the exclusion of implementation or professional services fees, shall be flagged for review and require written approval from both the CISO and VP of IT Procurement, in consultation with Meridian\'s General Counsel.
590	
591	**[9.2 Carve-Outs from Consequential Damages Exclusion]{.underline}**
592	
593	While the vendor agreement may include a mutual exclusion of consequential, indirect, incidental, special, and punitive damages as a general matter, the following categories of claims **shall be carved out** from any such exclusion and shall be subject to the full liability cap or, where specified below, unlimited liability:
594	
595	> \(a\) **Data Breaches.** Claims arising from unauthorized access to, acquisition of, disclosure of, or loss of Customer Data or PHI, including all costs of notification, credit monitoring, forensic investigation, regulatory defense, and penalties.
596	>
597	> \(b\) **Violations of the Business Associate Agreement.** Claims arising from the vendor\'s breach of the BAA, including but not limited to failure to comply with HIPAA and HITECH Act breach notification requirements, unauthorized use or disclosure of PHI, and failure to implement required safeguards.
598	>
599	> \(c\) **Infringement of Third-Party Intellectual Property Rights.** Claims arising from the vendor\'s infringement, misappropriation, or violation of third-party intellectual property rights through the vendor\'s platform, services, or deliverables.
600	>
601	> \(d\) **Willful Misconduct or Gross Negligence.** Claims arising from the vendor\'s willful misconduct or gross negligence. To the extent the vendor\'s willful misconduct or gross negligence causes loss to Meridian, such claims shall not be subject to any liability cap --- liability shall be **unlimited** for willful misconduct and gross negligence.
602	>

603	> \(e\) **Breach of Confidentiality Obligations.** Claims arising from the vendor\'s unauthorized disclosure or use of Meridian\'s confidential information, trade secrets, or proprietary data.
604	
605	The vendor agreement shall not apply a blanket mutual consequential damages exclusion without the foregoing carve-outs. Any proposed vendor agreement containing an unqualified consequential damages exclusion shall be returned to the vendor for negotiation of the required carve-outs.
606	
607	**[Section 10 --- Termination]{.underline}**
608	
609	**[10.1 Termination for Material Breach]{.underline}**
610	
611	Meridian shall have the right to terminate the vendor agreement if the vendor commits a material breach of any provision of the agreement and fails to cure such breach within **thirty (30) days** after receiving written notice of the breach from Meridian. For purposes of this section, \"material breach\" includes, without limitation: failure to meet uptime commitments for any two (2) consecutive months; failure to comply with security obligations set forth in the agreement or the BAA; breach of the BAA; unauthorized use or disclosure of Customer Data; failure to provide transition assistance; and failure to comply with applicable law or regulation.
612	
613	Upon termination for material breach, the vendor shall not be entitled to any termination fee, early termination penalty, or payment for services not yet rendered. The vendor\'s data retrieval and transition assistance obligations under Sections 7.2 and 7.3 shall apply.
614	
615	**[10.2 Termination for Convenience]{.underline}**
616	
617	Meridian shall have the right to terminate the vendor agreement for convenience upon **ninety (90) days\' prior written notice** to the vendor. **No termination fee, early termination penalty, or remaining-term fee obligation** shall apply to a termination for convenience by Meridian. The vendor shall be entitled to payment only for services actually rendered through the effective date of termination, plus any pre-paid fees for services not yet rendered, which shall be refunded to Meridian on a pro-rata basis.
618	
619	Upon termination for convenience, the vendor\'s data retrieval and transition assistance obligations under Sections 7.2 and 7.3 shall apply in full. The vendor shall cooperate fully with Meridian to ensure an orderly transition.
620	
621	**[10.3 Termination for Chronic SLA Failure]{.underline}**
622	
623	If the vendor fails to meet the applicable uptime commitment, response time commitments, or resolution time commitments in **three (3) or more months within any rolling six (6)-month period** (\"Chronic SLA Failure\"), Meridian shall have the right to terminate the vendor agreement **immediately upon written notice**, with **no cure period and no termination fee**. For purposes of this section, each calendar month in which the vendor fails to meet any one or more of the applicable commitments shall count as a separate month of failure.
624	
625	This termination right is in addition to, and not in limitation of, Meridian\'s rights to service credits under Section 4, actual damages under Section 4.3, and any other remedies available at law or in equity.
626	
627	**[10.4 Termination for Data Breach]{.underline}**
628	
629	If the vendor suffers a data breach, security incident, or unauthorized disclosure affecting Meridian\'s PHI or Customer Data, Meridian shall have the right to terminate the vendor agreement **immediately upon written notice**. The vendor shall have a **ten (10)-day cure period** from receipt of such notice, but only if all of the following conditions are satisfied:
630	
631	> \(a\) the vendor demonstrates to Meridian\'s reasonable satisfaction that the breach has been fully contained and that the threat vector has been eliminated;
632	>
633	> \(b\) the vendor has notified all affected individuals and regulatory authorities in compliance with HIPAA (45 CFR §§ 164.400--414), the HITECH Act (42 U.S.C. § 17932), and all applicable state breach notification laws; and
634	>
635	> \(c\) the vendor has implemented remedial measures reasonably satisfactory to Meridian to prevent recurrence, as documented in a written remediation plan provided to Meridian within the cure period.
636	
637	If the vendor fails to satisfy all three conditions within the ten (10)-day cure period, termination shall be effective automatically with no further action required by Meridian. **No termination fee, early termination penalty, or remaining-term fee obligation** shall apply to a termination under this Section 10.4.
638	
639	**[10.5 Effect of Termination]{.underline}**
640	
641	Upon termination or expiration of the vendor agreement for any reason, the following provisions shall survive and remain in full force and effect: data ownership (Section 7.1); data retrieval (Section 7.2); transition assistance (Section 7.3); limitation of liability (Section 9); confidentiality obligations; indemnification obligations; insurance obligations; any accrued but unpaid service credits; and any provisions that by their nature are intended to survive termination. The vendor shall cooperate fully with Meridian during the post-termination period to ensure an orderly transition and the complete retrieval of all Customer Data.
642	
643	**[Section 11 --- Audit Rights]{.underline}**
644	
645	**[11.1 Frequency and Notice]{.underline}**
646	
647	Meridian shall have the right to audit the vendor\'s compliance with the vendor agreement, including security obligations, BAA requirements, SLA performance, data handling practices, and subcontractor management, **no fewer than two (2) times per calendar year**. Meridian shall provide the vendor with no less than **thirty (30) days\' prior written notice** before conducting a scheduled audit.
648	
649	In addition, Meridian may conduct additional audits outside the two-per-year schedule upon reasonable cause, including but not limited to: following a security incident, data breach, or suspected non-compliance; following a change in the vendor\'s subcontractors, hosting locations, or key personnel; or in connection with a regulatory inquiry or investigation. For cause-based audits, Meridian shall provide reasonable notice under the circumstances, which may be less than thirty (30) days.
650	
651	**[11.2 Scope of Audit]{.underline}**
652	
653	Audits conducted under this section may include, without limitation:
654	
655	> \(a\) review of the vendor\'s policies, procedures, and technical controls related to data security, privacy, access management, and system availability;
656	>
657	> \(b\) review of the vendor\'s SOC 2 Type II reports, HITRUST CSF certification documentation, penetration testing reports, and vulnerability scanning results;
658	>
659	> \(c\) **physical inspection of data center facilities** where Meridian\'s Customer Data is hosted, processed, or stored, subject to the data center operator\'s reasonable physical security protocols and with reasonable advance coordination;
660	>
661	> \(d\) interviews with vendor personnel responsible for security, operations, incident response, and compliance functions;
662	>
663	> \(e\) review of system logs, access control records, authentication records, monitoring dashboards, and change management records;
664	>
665	> \(f\) **review of subcontractor compliance**, including the right to audit subcontractors\' facilities, records, and security controls to the same extent as the vendor\'s own, either directly or through the vendor; and
666	>
667	> \(g\) testing of disaster recovery and business continuity plans and capabilities.
668	
669	The vendor **shall not satisfy its audit obligations solely by providing a SOC 2 Type II report** or any other single certification document or third-party assessment. While such reports may supplement and inform the audit process, Meridian retains the absolute right to conduct independent verification of the vendor\'s compliance through direct inspection, testing, and review.
670	
671	**[11.3 Cost of Audits]{.underline}**
672	
673	Meridian shall bear the costs of routine audits, including the fees of any third-party auditors engaged by Meridian to conduct or assist with the audit. The vendor shall make its personnel, facilities, records, and systems reasonably available to support the audit at no additional charge to Meridian.
674	
675	However, if an audit reveals **material non-compliance** with the vendor agreement, including security standards, SLA commitments, BAA obligations, or any other material provision, the vendor shall:
676	
677	> \(a\) **reimburse Meridian for all costs of the audit** that identified the non-compliance, including fees of third-party auditors, travel expenses, and internal personnel costs; and
678	>
679	> \(b\) **bear all costs of remediation** required to bring the vendor into compliance, including the cost of implementing corrective actions, retesting, and follow-up audits.
680	
681	\"Material non-compliance\" means any finding that, if left unaddressed, would: (i) create a reasonable risk of unauthorized access to, disclosure of, or loss of PHI; (ii) result in a breach of the BAA; (iii) constitute a failure to meet applicable uptime commitments; or (iv) violate applicable law or regulation.
682	
683	**[Section 12 --- Governing Law and Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**
684	
685	**[12.1 Governing Law]{.underline}**
686	
687	All vendor agreements subject to these Standards shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the **State of North Carolina**, without giving effect to any choice-of-law or conflict-of-law provisions that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. The vendor agreement shall not specify any governing law other than North Carolina law without the prior written approval of Meridian\'s General Counsel.
688	
689	**[12.2 Jurisdiction and Venue]{.underline}**
690	
691	The vendor agreement shall provide that any disputes, claims, or controversies arising out of or relating to the agreement, including its formation, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination, shall be resolved through **litigation in the state or federal courts located in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina**. Each party shall irrevocably consent to the exclusive personal jurisdiction and venue of such courts and shall waive any objection based on inconvenient forum or lack of jurisdiction.
692	
693	The parties may agree to include a **non-binding mediation** step as a precursor to litigation, to be conducted by a mutually agreed mediator in Charlotte, North Carolina. However, mediation shall not be a mandatory prerequisite to filing suit, and neither party shall be required to delay the filing of a lawsuit pending the completion of mediation.
694	
695	**[12.3 Prohibition on Mandatory Arbitration]{.underline}**
696	
697	**The vendor agreement shall not include any mandatory binding arbitration clause for disputes with an amount in controversy exceeding one million dollars (\$1,000,000).** Meridian\'s policy is to preserve its right to litigate material disputes before a court of competent jurisdiction with full discovery rights, appellate review, and the protections afforded by the rules of civil procedure.
698	
699	For disputes with an amount in controversy of one million dollars (\$1,000,000) or less, the parties may agree to binding arbitration under mutually agreed rules, provided that: (a) the arbitration shall be seated in Charlotte, North Carolina; (b) the arbitration shall be governed by North Carolina law; and (c) the arbitrator shall have expertise in healthcare information technology or healthcare regulatory matters.
700	
701	**Jury trial waivers are permissible** only if mutually agreed, expressly bargained for, and set forth in a separately executed waiver document, rather than embedded in a standard form agreement.
702

This Exhibit A is attached to and incorporated by reference into the Master SaaS Agreement (the \"**Agreement**\") entered into as of November 4, 2025, by and between Cloudvance Technologies, Inc. **[A.1 Platform Description]{.underline}**

The ClinicalEdge™ Platform is a comprehensive, cloud-based, multi-tenant software-as-a-service solution designed for healthcare organizations. The Platform includes the following core modules, each of which is included in Customer\'s subscription:

> **(a) Electronic Health Records (EHR) Module.** A fully integrated electronic health records system supporting clinical documentation, order entry (CPOE), medication management, allergy tracking, problem lists, immunization records, patient history, and clinical notes across inpatient and outpatient settings. The EHR Module is designed to meet Meaningful Use / Promoting Interoperability requirements and supports interoperability through industry-standard HL7 and FHIR protocols.
>
> **(b) Clinical Decision Support Module.** Evidence-based clinical decision support tools integrated into the EHR workflow, including drug-drug interaction alerts, drug-allergy interaction alerts, clinical guidelines, care pathway recommendations, diagnostic support tools, and configurable alert rules. The Clinical Decision Support Module leverages Cloudvance\'s proprietary clinical knowledge base, which is updated on a quarterly basis.
>
> **(c) Patient Portal Module.** A secure, patient-facing web and mobile application enabling patients to access their health records, view lab results, request prescription refills, schedule appointments, communicate with their care team via secure messaging, and complete pre-visit forms and questionnaires. The Patient Portal is accessible via standard web browsers and native iOS and Android mobile applications.
>
> **(d) Revenue Cycle Management Module.** An integrated revenue cycle management solution supporting charge capture, claims submission, remittance processing, denial management, patient billing, payment posting, and financial reporting. The data migration shall include patient demographics, encounter histories, clinical notes, medication records, allergy records, problem lists, immunization records, lab results, imaging reports, billing records, and other data categories as mutually agreed upon by the Parties. Cloudvance shall develop a detailed data migration plan, including data mapping specifications, data validation procedures, and reconciliation protocols, and shall conduct test migrations prior to the final production migration.
>
> **(b) System Configuration and Customization.** Cloudvance shall configure the ClinicalEdge Platform to align with Customer\'s clinical workflows, operational processes, and organizational structure. Configuration activities shall include, without limitation, departmental and facility setup, user role and permission configurations, order set creation, clinical template customization, report configuration, and integration of Customer-specific clinical protocols and care pathways.
>
> **(c) Integration.** Cloudvance shall integrate the ClinicalEdge Platform with Customer\'s existing clinical and administrative information systems, including laboratory information systems, pharmacy information systems, radiology information systems, picture archiving and communication systems (PACS), billing and practice management systems, and other third-party systems as identified during the implementation planning phase. Integrations shall utilize HL7 v2.x, FHIR R4, and other industry-standard interface protocols as appropriate. Customer currently operates eleven (11) hospitals and forty-seven (47) outpatient clinics across North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia, and the integration scope encompasses all such facilities.
>
> **(d) Training.** Cloudvance shall provide comprehensive end-user training for up to five hundred (500) Authorized Users in the initial deployment phase, utilizing a train-the-trainer methodology supplemented by e-learning modules, on-site classroom sessions, and go-live at-the-elbow support. Training shall cover all core Platform modules and shall be tailored to the roles and responsibilities of the respective user groups (e.g., physicians, nurses, clinical support staff, administrative staff, revenue cycle personnel).
>
> **(e) Go-Live Support.** Cloudvance shall provide dedicated on-site and remote go-live support for a period of thirty (30) days following the Go-Live Date to assist Customer with issue resolution, workflow optimization, and user adoption during the initial production period.

The target Go-Live Date for production deployment is July 1, 2026, subject to the terms set forth in Section 3.3 of the Agreement.

**[A.3 Support Services]{.underline}**

> **(a) Standard Support Hours.** Cloudvance shall provide technical support via telephone and electronic mail during standard business hours of 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM Eastern Time, Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays observed by Cloudvance.
>
> **(b) Critical Incident Support.** For incidents classified as Critical (as defined in Exhibit C, Section C.7), Cloudvance shall provide twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week support via a dedicated emergency hotline. Customer shall be provided with the emergency hotline number upon execution of this Agreement and upon any subsequent changes to such number.
>
> **(c) Response and Resolution Times.** Incident response and resolution time targets are set forth in Exhibit C, Section C.7. Cloudvance shall classify incidents in accordance with the severity levels defined therein and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to respond to and resolve incidents within the applicable time targets.
>
> **(d) Software Updates.** During the Subscription Term, Cloudvance shall make available to Customer all updates, upgrades, patches, and new releases to the Platform that Cloudvance makes generally available to its customers at no additional charge, subject to Cloudvance\'s standard release management and deployment procedures.

The initial deployment of the ClinicalEdge Platform under this Agreement covers up to five thousand (5,000) Authorized Users across Customer\'s healthcare facilities. Additional Authorized Users may be added by Customer from time to time pursuant to a written order form executed by both Parties, at then-current per-user rates as published by Cloudvance or as otherwise agreed upon in writing by the Parties. from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT

def new_doc():
    d = Document()
    for s in d.sections:
        s.left_margin = s.right_margin = Inches(1)
        s.top_margin = s.bottom_margin = Inches(1)
    st = d.styles["Normal"]
    st.font.name = "Calibri"; st.font.size = Pt(11)
    st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Calibri")
    for n, sz in (("Heading 1", 14), ("Heading 2", 12), ("Heading 3", 11)):

def shade(cell, hexcolor):

    tcPr.append(shd)

def add_runs(p, text):
    # simple **bold** markup
    parts = text.split("**")
    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
        if not part: continue
        r = p.add_run(part)
        if i % 2 == 1: r.bold = True
    return p

    p = d.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else d.add_paragraph()
    add_runs(p, text)
    if italic:
        for r in p.runs: r.italic = True
    if size:
        for r in p.runs: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    if align: p.alignment = align
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    return p

def bullet(d, text, level=0):
    p = d.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet" if level == 0 else "List Bullet 2")
    add_runs(p, text); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    return p

def numbered(d, text):
    p = d.add_paragraph(style="List Number"); add_runs(p, text); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3); return p

def table(d, header, rows, widths=None, risk_col=None, font=9):
    t = d.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(header))
    t.style = "Table Grid"; t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i, h in enumerate(header):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text = ""
        r = c.paragraphs[0].add_run(h); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(font); r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
        shade(c, "1F3A5F")
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, v in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ""
            add_runs(cells[i].paragraphs[0], str(v))
            for r in cells[i].paragraphs[0].runs: r.font.size = Pt(font)
            if risk_col is not None and i == risk_col and v in RISK_COLORS:
                for r in cells[i].paragraphs[0].runs:
                    r.bold = True; r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(RISK_COLORS[v])
    # repeat header
    trPr = t.rows[0]._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); th = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"); th.set(qn("w:val"), "true"); trPr.append(th)
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    d.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

def gap(d, g):
    d.add_heading(g["id"] + "  " + g["title"], level=3)
    t = d.add_table(rows=0, cols=2); t.style = "Table Grid"
    def row(label, text, color=None):
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        cells[0].text = ""; r = cells[0].paragraphs[0].add_run(label); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(9.5); shade(cells[0], "DCE6F1")
        cells[1].text = ""
        paras = text if isinstance(text, list) else [text]
        for j, tx in enumerate(paras):
            p = cells[1].paragraphs[0] if j == 0 else cells[1].add_paragraph()
            add_runs(p, tx)
            for rr in p.runs:
                rr.font.size = Pt(9.5)
                if color: rr.bold = True; rr.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
        cells[0].width = Inches(1.45); cells[1].width = Inches(5.05)
    row("Risk rating", g["risk"], RISK_COLORS.get(g["risk"]))
    row("SLS v4.2 requirement", g["sls"])
    row("Agreement provision", g["agr"])
    row("Gap / analysis", g["gap"])
    row("Recommended redline", g["redline"])
    row("Negotiation position", g["position"])
    d.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
EOF
echo ok'

dict(id="D-2", title="BAA breach notification (30 days) and permitted uses (data aggregation, de-identification)", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §5.1: any actual or suspected PHI compromise is an S1 incident, with a 15-minute response and status updates every 30 minutes. SLS §10.4(b) assumes the vendor notifies individuals and regulators in compliance with 45 CFR §§164.400 to 414, 42 U.S.C. §17932 and state law. SLS §6.5 limits de-identified data to uses that **directly benefit Meridian**, with prior consent, opt-out rights and methodology documentation.",
 agr="Ex. D §D.5: notice of a Breach of Unsecured PHI is due within **30 days** of discovery. §D.4(c) permits Data Aggregation for Meridian\x27s health care operations. §D.4(d) permits use of De-Identified Data \"as set forth in Section 6.3 of the Agreement,\" which allows product improvement, analytics, research, product development and pooling with other customers\x27 data.",
 gap=["**Notification.** Thirty days is within the HIPAA outer limit for business associates (60 days, 45 CFR §164.410), but it is out of step with an S1 classification for suspected PHI compromise. It also uses up half of Meridian\x27s own 60-day clock to notify individuals under 45 CFR §164.404, and it may conflict with the shorter regulator-notice expectations under state law (for example, notification to the NC Attorney General under N.C. Gen. Stat. §75-65). Notice of Security Incidents has no deadline at all (see D-1).",
  "**Permitted uses.** Under 45 CFR §164.502(d) and §164.504(e)(2)(i), a business associate may de-identify PHI only if the BAA permits it. §D.4(d) is therefore the legal authorization for Cloudvance\x27s data program, which makes it the most consequential sentence in the BAA. It must be narrowed in line with SLS §6.5."],
 redline="Amend §D.5: \"Business Associate shall notify Covered Entity\x27s CISO by telephone and email **without unreasonable delay and in no event later than twenty-four (24) hours** after discovery of any actual or suspected Breach of Unsecured PHI or Security Incident (excluding unsuccessful attempts that do not penetrate Business Associate\x27s systems, such as pings and port scans), and shall provide the information required by 45 CFR §164.410(c) within five (5) business days thereafter, supplementing it as more information becomes available. Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity for all costs of notification, credit monitoring, call center, forensic investigation and regulatory response arising from any Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.\" Replace §D.4(d): \"Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with 45 CFR §164.514(b), and may use De-Identified Data only for the purposes, and subject to the conditions, set forth in Section 6.3 of the Agreement (as amended).\"",
 position="A 24-hour initial notice is the market norm for hospital customers and follows from the S1 classification. If Cloudvance resists, 72 hours is an acceptable fallback, because the SLS does not fix an exact BAA notice period."),

dict(id="D-3", title="Encryption: \"industry-standard\" language that the SLS prohibits", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §6.2: **AES-256** at rest across all storage tiers, including backups and DR copies. **TLS 1.2 or higher** in transit on all networks, with SSL, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 disabled. Key management per **NIST SP 800-57**, with at least annual key rotation and separation of duties. Vague terms such as \"industry-standard encryption\" are prohibited, and algorithms and key lengths must be stated in the agreement.",
 agr="Ex. E §E.3: Cloudvance shall encrypt Customer Data \"using **industry-standard encryption** both at rest and in transit.\" Key management only restricts access to keys to \"authorized personnel.\" Ex. E §E.6 applies \"the same encryption standards\" to backups.",
 gap="The Agreement uses the exact wording SLS §6.2 prohibits. No algorithm, key length, protocol version or key-management standard is stated. Encryption also matters for HIPAA purposes: PHI encrypted in line with HHS guidance is not \"Unsecured PHI,\" so a weak or undefined standard increases the likelihood that a security incident becomes a reportable breach.",
 redline="Replace §E.3: \"Cloudvance shall, and shall cause its Subcontractors to, (a) encrypt all Customer Data at rest, including primary, secondary, archival, backup and disaster-recovery copies, using **AES with a 256-bit key (AES-256)** or a successor standard approved in writing by Customer\x27s CISO; (b) encrypt all Customer Data in transit over any network, including internal networks and inter-data-center links, using **TLS 1.2 or higher**, and disable SSL (all versions), TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 on all systems and endpoints that process Customer Data; and (c) manage encryption keys in accordance with **NIST SP 800-57**, including rotation at least annually (and promptly upon any suspected compromise) and separation of duties between key custodians and system administrators.\"",
 position="Must-have. These are almost certainly existing Cloudvance practices, so the main task is to have them written into the contract. We recommend asking Cloudvance and Stratos to confirm their current cipher suites during diligence."),

dict(id="D-4", title="Security certifications and testing: SOC 2 only; no HITRUST, penetration testing or vulnerability scanning", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §6.3: (a) a **SOC 2 Type II** report covering all five Trust Services Criteria, issued within the prior 12 months and covering all systems and data centers, provided annually; (b) **HITRUST CSF certification**, current at signing and maintained throughout the term; (c) **annual independent penetration test**, with the full report within 30 days; (d) **quarterly vulnerability scans**, with results on request.",
 agr="Ex. E §E.2: Cloudvance \"maintains SOC 2 Type II certification\" and will provide its most recent report within 30 days of request. It will notify Meridian of a lapse or material deficiency. The Agreement does not mention HITRUST, penetration testing or vulnerability scanning.",
 gap="Dr. Nandakumar\x27s concern is confirmed: HITRUST CSF is required by SLS §6.3(b) (added in v4.1) and is entirely absent. The SOC 2 commitment does not specify scope (which Trust Services Criteria; whether it covers Stratos-hosted environments, either directly or through carve-out or inclusive treatment of the subservice organization), currency, or annual delivery. SOC 2 is an attestation report, not a \"certification\"; the wording should be corrected so that the obligation is clear. There is no right to penetration test results or scan data.",
 redline="Replace §E.2: \"Cloudvance shall obtain and maintain throughout the Term: (a) a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality and Privacy Trust Services Criteria, issued by an independent auditor within the preceding twelve (12) months and covering all systems, data centers (including those of Stratos and any other hosting Subcontractor) and processes used to provide the Services; and (b) a validated **HITRUST CSF certification** covering the Platform and related healthcare systems, current as of the Effective Date. Cloudvance shall deliver current copies to Customer at least annually and on request. Cloudvance shall engage an independent, unaffiliated firm to perform penetration testing of all systems processing Customer Data at least annually and shall deliver the full report, including findings, risk ratings and remediation plans, within thirty (30) days of completion. Cloudvance shall perform internal and external vulnerability scans at least quarterly and provide results and remediation status on request.\"",
 position="Must-have. If Cloudvance does not currently hold HITRUST CSF certification, a time-limited path (for example, HITRUST r2 certification within 12 months of the Effective Date, with a termination right if it is not achieved) would be a deviation requiring CISO and VP approval. Ask Cloudvance now whether it is certified."),

dict(id="D-5", title="Safeguards described as \"commercially reasonable\"; several required controls missing", risk="Medium",
 sls="SLS §6.4: safeguards must meet the HIPAA Security Rule (§§164.308, 164.310, 164.312) **and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework**, specified \"with particularity,\" with no \"commercially reasonable\" or \"appropriate\" language. Minimum controls: MFA for administrative, privileged **and remote** access; RBAC with least privilege; audit logs retained for 12 months; **IDS/IPS**; **EDR**; **network segmentation of PHI systems**; IR plan tested annually; DR/BCP tested annually **with results reported to Meridian**.",
 agr="Ex. E §E.1: \"commercially reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards.\" §E.4: RBAC, MFA for administrative and privileged access, unique IDs, session timeouts, and logging with one-year retention. §E.5: a written IR plan, but no testing requirement. §E.6: DR plan tested annually, with a summary \"upon request\"; RTO of 24 hours and RPO of 4 hours stated as \"targets.\" §D.3(b): \"appropriate\" safeguards.",
 gap="The Agreement meets the SLS on RBAC, administrative and privileged MFA, and 12-month log retention. It falls short on: the \"commercially reasonable\" and \"appropriate\" qualifiers; NIST CSF alignment; MFA for remote access; IDS/IPS; EDR; network segmentation; annual IR plan testing; and proactive reporting of DR test results. **Additional observation (not an SLS requirement):** a 24-hour RTO for a Tier 1 EHR is inconsistent with the SLS 4-hour S1 resolution commitment, and a 4-hour RPO could mean losing up to four hours of clinical documentation and medication orders. ClinicalEdge is multi-tenant (Ex. A §A.1), which makes logical segregation of Meridian\x27s data important.",
 redline="Replace \"commercially reasonable\" in §E.1 with \"administrative, technical and physical safeguards that meet or exceed the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR §§164.308, 164.310, 164.312) and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (current version), including at a minimum the controls in Section E.4.\" Expand §E.4 to add MFA for remote access, least privilege, IDS/IPS, EDR on all systems processing Customer Data, segmentation of PHI systems and logical tenant isolation. Add annual tabletop or simulation testing of the IR plan, and annual DR/BCP testing with results delivered to Customer. Make RTO and RPO binding commitments; we recommend an RTO of 4 hours or less and an RPO of 15 minutes or less for Tier 1, subject to Meridian clinical and IT confirmation.",
 position="Must-have for removing the vague qualifiers and adding the listed controls. The RTO and RPO numbers are a recommendation for Meridian IT to set."),

dict(id="D-6", title="Cyber liability insurance: no minimum, no coverage terms", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §6.6: cyber and technology E&O coverage of at least **$10,000,000 per occurrence and in the aggregate**, covering breach response, regulatory defense and penalties, business interruption (including Meridian\x27s losses), network security liability and media liability. Meridian named as **additional insured** where permissible. A **certificate of insurance** at execution, at each renewal and on request. **30 days\x27 notice** of cancellation, non-renewal or material reduction. SLS §10.5: insurance obligations survive.",
 agr="§12, in full: \"Each Party shall maintain commercially reasonable insurance coverage appropriate to its business and operations throughout the Term of this Agreement.\"",
 gap="Marcus Ellison correctly identified this gap. The Agreement sets no limits and no coverage types, and has no additional-insured, certificate or notice requirement. Because the liability cap is $6.84M (see F-1), Meridian has no assurance that Cloudvance could pay a large breach claim. Industry data put the average healthcare breach cost well above most mid-market vendors\x27 balance-sheet capacity. The clause is also mutual, which imposes an undefined insurance obligation on Meridian.",
 redline="Replace §12: \"Cloudvance shall maintain throughout the Term and for three (3) years thereafter, with insurers rated A- VII or better by A.M. Best: (a) cyber liability / technology errors and omissions insurance with limits of not less than **$10,000,000 per occurrence and in the aggregate**, covering data breach response costs (notification, credit monitoring, identity remediation, call center, forensics), regulatory defense and penalties (including HHS OCR and State attorneys general), business interruption (including Customer\x27s lost revenue and extra expense), network security liability and media liability; and (b) commercial general liability insurance in customary amounts. Customer shall be named as an additional insured where permissible. Cloudvance shall deliver certificates of insurance at execution, upon each renewal and upon request, and shall provide at least thirty (30) days\x27 prior written notice of cancellation, non-renewal or material reduction in coverage.\" Delete the mutual obligation on Customer, or limit it to customary coverage.",
 position="Must-have. Limits above $10M should be considered given the size of the patient population. The $10M SLS figure is a floor."),
]

  "Replace §6.3: \"Cloudvance may de-identify Customer Data in accordance with 45 CFR §164.514(b) or (c), and may use such De-Identified Data **only to provide analytics, reporting, benchmarking and dashboards to Customer** in connection with the Services. Customer may opt out of any de-identified data use on written notice, and Cloudvance shall cease such use within thirty (30) days. Cloudvance shall document its de-identification methodology and make that documentation available to Customer on request.\" Delete §6.4, or fold it into §6.3 under the same limits.  position="Must-have for the §6.2 license limits and the §6.3 consent and opt-out mechanics. If Meridian\x27s business leadership sees value in a specific benchmarking program, the right approach is for Meridian to grant a separate written consent for a defined use, which SLS §6.5(b) permits, rather than to accept the broad grant in the draft."),

dict(id="E-3", title="Post-termination data retrieval: 30 days, unspecified format, Meridian solely responsible", risk="Critical",
 sls="SLS §7.2: a Data Retrieval Period of at least **90 days** after termination or expiration for any reason. During that period, data must be kept secure. Data must be delivered in **HL7 FHIR** for clinical data and **CSV** for administrative and financial data, or other formats Meridian specifies, at no charge. After retrieval, destruction in line with **NIST SP 800-88**, with an officer-signed **certificate of destruction within 15 days**. SLS §7.1: no copies retained after the Retrieval Period except as required by law.",
 agr="§6.5: data is available \"for download by Customer in a **commercially standard format**\" for **30 days**. \"Customer shall be **solely responsible** for downloading and retrieving.\" Afterward, Cloudvance has no obligation and \"may, **in its sole discretion**, delete\" the data. Deletion is confirmed in writing only \"upon Customer\x27s request.\" §5.3 permits retention \"as part of its standard backup and archival procedures.\" §11.5(a): all access rights terminate immediately. §D.6: return or destruction \"if feasible.\"",

  "\"Commercially standard format\" could be satisfied by flat files or proprietary database dumps. FHIR is not guaranteed, even though Cloudvance supports FHIR R4 interfaces (Ex. A §A.2(c)). That is inconsistent with SLS §7.1 and with the HIPAA return-or-destroy principle.",
  "Medical record retention obligations make this especially sensitive. Meridian must be able to produce complete records for many years after the relationship ends."],
 redline="Replace §6.5: \"Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Cloudvance shall make all Customer Data available to Customer for a period of not less than **ninety (90) days** (the \"Data Retrieval Period\"), during which Cloudvance shall continue to maintain the Customer Data in accordance with all security obligations of this Agreement and the BAA. SLS §10.1: failure to provide transition assistance is a material breach.",
 agr="The Agreement contains no transition assistance obligation. §11.5(a) cuts off Platform access immediately on termination. The only post-termination obligation is the 30-day download window in §6.5.",

 redline="Insert new §11.7 and Exhibit F (Transition Assistance Plan): \"Upon expiration or any termination (including termination by Cloudvance for Customer\x27s breach), and upon Customer\x27s request, Cloudvance shall provide transition assistance for up to twelve (12) months in accordance with Exhibit F, including continued operation of the Platform at the service levels in Exhibit C during any parallel-operations period, at the rates in Exhibit F (not to exceed Cloudvance\x27s then-current published professional services rates, and escalating by no more than 3% per year). Cloudvance shall not condition transition assistance on payment of any termination fee or disputed amount.\" Exhibit F should list named transition roles, milestones, deliverables (data dictionaries, ERDs, API specifications) and the API access to be provided.",
 position="Must-have. The plan exhibit will take time to negotiate, so we recommend starting it now rather than leaving it for after signing."),
