dict(id="S-1", title="Subcontractor engagement: notice after the fact instead of prior written consent", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §8.1: **prior written consent** for any subcontractor or sub-processor that touches Customer Data, requested at least **30 days before** engagement. The request must include identity and location, data scope, SOC 2, HITRUST and penetration testing status, and a copy of the subcontract or DPA. Meridian may **object within 15 days**, and the vendor may then not use the subcontractor. Engaging a subcontractor without consent is a **material breach**.",
 agr="§7.1: Cloudvance may engage new or replacement Subcontractors \"without the prior written consent of Customer,\" giving notice **within 30 days after** engagement. Meridian\x27s \"**sole remedy**\" is to object within 15 days, after which the parties \"confer in good faith.\" Stratos is acknowledged as the incumbent hosting Subcontractor.",
 gap="Meridian could first learn of a new PHI sub-processor, including an offshore support vendor, up to 30 days after that vendor has started handling Meridian\x27s data. Meridian would have no right to block it. This is the reverse of the SLS model. The §7.1 acknowledgment also pre-approves Stratos without any of the diligence materials SLS §8.1 requires.",
 redline="Replace the third through fifth sentences of §7.1: \"Cloudvance shall not engage any Subcontractor that will access, process, store or transmit Customer Data without Customer\x27s **prior written consent**. Cloudvance shall submit a request at least thirty (30) days before the proposed engagement, including the Subcontractor\x27s legal name, principal place of business and service locations, the scope of Customer Data involved, its SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST CSF and recent penetration testing results, and a copy of the proposed subcontract or BAA. Customer may object within fifteen (15) days of receiving a complete request, in which case Cloudvance shall not use that Subcontractor for Customer Data. Engagement of a Subcontractor in breach of this Section is a material breach.\" Make Customer\x27s acceptance of Stratos conditional on delivery of the SLS §8.1(a) to (d) materials before signing.",
 position="Must-have. Cloudvance may push back that a multi-tenant platform cannot accommodate customer-specific vetoes. A possible deviation (requiring CISO and VP approval) would be a right to terminate without fee if Meridian reasonably objects and Cloudvance proceeds anyway."),

dict(id="S-2", title="Flow-down obligations and Stratos visibility", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §8.2: subcontract terms must be **at least as protective** as the vendor agreement, covering (a) security, privacy and HIPAA/HITECH, including a **subcontractor BAA**; (b) the **same service levels**; (c) **audit rights for Meridian**; (d) data handling, portability and destruction; and (e) confidentiality. The vendor is fully liable for subcontractors, must make subcontracts available on request and must notify Meridian of subcontractor breaches.",
 agr="§7.2: Cloudvance is responsible and liable for Subcontractors and will enter into agreements \"**sufficient to enable Cloudvance to comply** with its obligations.\" §D.3(d): PHI subcontractors agree in writing to \"the same restrictions, conditions, and requirements\" as the BAA.",
 gap="The liability language in §7.2 and the PHI flow-down in §D.3(d) meet part of the SLS. The \"sufficient to enable\" standard is weaker than \"at least as protective.\" There is also no flow-down of service levels, Meridian audit rights or destruction obligations, and no right to review the Stratos agreement. The value of §7.2 is reduced by §15.1, which treats hosting failures as force majeure (A-6), and by §C.7, which extends resolution times when resolution depends on third-party vendors.",
 redline="Amend the last sentence of §7.2: \"Cloudvance shall bind each Subcontractor by written agreement to obligations **at least as protective of Customer** as those in this Agreement, including a subcontractor business associate agreement compliant with HIPAA/HITECH, service level commitments sufficient to support Exhibit C, audit rights exercisable by Cloudvance and Customer, and the data handling, portability, destruction and confidentiality obligations of this Agreement. Cloudvance shall make such agreements available to Customer on request and shall promptly notify Customer of any Subcontractor breach or non-compliance affecting Customer Data. Failures of Subcontractors shall not excuse Cloudvance\x27s performance.\"",
 position="Must-have. As part of diligence, request the Stratos SOC 2 and HITRUST reports, the Cloudvance–Stratos BAA and the data center list now."),

dict(id="S-3", title="Hosting location: any Stratos U.S. data center, movable at Cloudvance\x27s discretion", risk="Medium",
 sls="SLS §8.3: data may be hosted only in locations **approved in writing and listed by city and state** in a schedule. Data may not be moved or replicated to an unlisted site without **90 days\x27 notice and consent**, which Meridian may withhold in its sole discretion. Data must remain in the **continental United States** and may not be hosted, processed, stored **or accessed** from outside it without consent.",
 agr="§7.3: data may be hosted in \"any Stratos Cloud Services data center located in the United States.\" Cloudvance may move data between Stratos U.S. data centers \"at its discretion.\" Transfer or storage outside the U.S. requires consent. §E.6: backups are kept in geographically separate Stratos U.S. locations.",
 gap="There is no schedule of approved sites, no notice or consent for moves, and no restriction on **remote access** from outside the U.S. (for example, by offshore support personnel). \"United States\" could include non-continental states and territories. Moving data within Stratos also changes the subcontractor risk profile without Meridian\x27s knowledge.",
 redline="Replace §7.3: \"Customer Data (including backups) shall be hosted, processed and stored only at the data center locations listed by city and state in **Schedule 7.3**, each approved in writing by Customer. Cloudvance shall not migrate, replicate or transfer Customer Data to any other location without at least ninety (90) days\x27 prior written notice and Customer\x27s prior written consent, which Customer may withhold in its sole discretion. Customer Data shall at all times remain within the continental United States and shall not be hosted, processed, stored or **accessed** from any location outside the continental United States without Customer\x27s prior written consent.\"",
 position="Must-have for the offshore-access restriction and the schedule of sites. On moves between listed Stratos sites, a 30-day notice period could be considered as a fallback, which would be a deviation."),
]

Deletion is confirmed in writing only \"upon Customer\x27s request.\" §5.3 permits retention \"as part of its standard backup and archival procedures.\" §11.5(a): all access rights terminate immediately. §D.6: return or destruction \"if feasible.\"",
 gap=["This is one of the most significant operational risks in the draft. Thirty days is one-third of the SLS minimum and is unrealistic for migrating the complete longitudinal records of hundreds of thousands of patients across 58 facilities. Meridian is experiencing that difficulty now with the LegacyMed exit.",
  "\"Commercially standard format\" could be satisfied by flat files or proprietary database dumps. FHIR is not guaranteed, even though Cloudvance supports FHIR R4 interfaces (Ex. A §A.2(c)). There is no export-fee prohibition and no successor-vendor cooperation. \"Sole discretion\" deletion, without a NIST 800-88 standard or a mandatory certificate, together with the backup-retention carve-out in §5.3, leaves PHI in Cloudvance\x27s backups indefinitely. That is inconsistent with SLS §7.1 and with the HIPAA return-or-destroy principle.",
  "Medical record retention obligations make this especially sensitive. Meridian must be able to produce complete records for many years after the relationship ends."],
 redline="Replace §6.5: \"Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Cloudvance shall make all Customer Data available to Customer for a period of not less than **ninety (90) days** (the \"Data Retrieval Period\"), during which Cloudvance shall continue to maintain the Customer Data in accordance with all security obligations of this Agreement and the BAA. At Customer\x27s request and at no additional charge, Cloudvance shall export Customer Data (a) in **HL7 FHIR** format (R4 or later) for all clinical data, patient records and health information, (b) in **CSV** format for administrative, financial and other non-clinical data, and (c) in such additional formats as Customer reasonably specifies, together with data dictionaries and schema documentation. Cloudvance shall cooperate fully with Customer and any successor vendor and shall confirm in writing when the export is complete. Following the Data Retrieval Period and Customer\x27s written confirmation that retrieval is complete, Cloudvance shall destroy all Customer Data, including backups, archives and disaster-recovery copies, in accordance with NIST SP 800-88, and shall deliver a certificate of destruction signed by an officer within fifteen (15) days of completion.\" Conform §5.3 (delete the backup-retention carve-out as applied to Customer Data), §11.5(c) and §D.6.",
 position="Must-have. We recommend also seeking a right to extend the Data Retrieval Period on a month-to-month basis at the then-current subscription rate while migration is underway (our recommendation; not an SLS requirement)."),

dict(id="E-4", title="No Transition Assistance Plan", risk="Critical",
 sls="SLS §7.3: a **Transition Assistance Plan** attached as an exhibit, providing up to **12 months** of assistance at pre-agreed rates. The plan must name dedicated personnel, set a timeline and milestones, provide data mapping and schema documentation (data dictionaries, ERDs, API specifications), API access and integration support, and **parallel operations** at agreed service levels. Assistance may **not be conditioned** on payment of termination fees or disputed amounts. Rates are capped at published or contract rates, with escalation of no more than 3% per year. SLS §10.1: failure to provide transition assistance is a material breach.",
 agr="The Agreement contains no transition assistance obligation. §11.5(a) cuts off Platform access immediately on termination. The only post-termination obligation is the 30-day download window in §6.5.",
 gap="An EHR cannot be switched off overnight. Without contractual transition support, Meridian would have little leverage at exit. Cloudvance could price transition services at will, or decline to provide them, while Meridian\x27s clinical operations depend on uninterrupted access. Under §4.4, Cloudvance could also suspend access over a payment dispute (see J-2).",
 redline="Insert new §11.7 and Exhibit F (Transition Assistance Plan): \"Upon expiration or any termination (including termination by Cloudvance for Customer\x27s breach), and upon Customer\x27s request, Cloudvance shall provide transition assistance for up to twelve (12) months in accordance with Exhibit F, including continued operation of the Platform at the service levels in Exhibit C during any parallel-operations period, at the rates in Exhibit F (not to exceed Cloudvance\x27s then-current published professional services rates, and escalating by no more than 3% per year). Cloudvance shall not condition transition assistance on payment of any termination fee or disputed amount.\" Exhibit F should list named transition roles, milestones, deliverables (data dictionaries, ERDs, API specifications) and the API access to be provided.",
 position="Must-have. The plan exhibit will take time to negotiate, so we recommend starting it now rather than leaving it for after signing."),

# ---------------- SUBCONTRACTORS ----------------
dict(id="S-1", title="Subcontractor engagement: notice after the fact instead of prior written consent", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §8.1: **prior written consent** for any subcontractor or sub-processor that touches Customer Data, requested at least **30 days before** engagement. The request must include identity and location, data scope, SOC 2, HITRUST and penetration testing status, and a copy of the subcontract or DPA. Meridian may **object within 15 days**, and the vendor may then not use the subcontractor. Engaging a subcontractor without consent is a **material breach**.",
 agr="§7.1: Cloudvance may engage new or replacement Subcontractors \"without the prior written consent of Customer,\" giving notice **within 30 days after** engagement. Meridian\x27s \"**sole remedy**\" is to object within 15 days, after which the parties \"confer in good faith.\" Stratos is acknowledged as the incumbent hosting Subcontractor.",
 gap="Meridian could first learn of a new PHI sub-processor, including an offshore support vendor, up to 30 days after that vendor has started handling Meridian\x27s data. Meridian would have no right to block it. This is the reverse of the SLS model. The §7.1 acknowledgment also pre-approves Stratos without any of the diligence materials SLS §8.1 requires.",
 redline="Replace the third through fifth sentences of §7.1: \"Cloudvance shall not engage any Subcontractor that will access, process, store or transmit Customer Data without Customer\x27s **prior written consent**. Cloudvance shall submit a request at least thirty (30) days before the proposed engagement, including the Subcontractor\x27s legal name, principal place of business and service locations, the scope of Customer Data involved, its SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST CSF and recent penetration testing results, and a copy of the proposed subcontract or BAA. Customer may object within fifteen (15) days of receiving a complete request, in which case Cloudvance shall not use that Subcontractor for Customer Data. Engagement of a Subcontractor in breach of this Section is a material breach.\" Make Customer\x27s acceptance of Stratos conditional on delivery of the SLS §8.1(a) to (d) materials before signing.",
 position="Must-have. Cloudvance may push back that a multi-tenant platform cannot accommodate customer-specific vetoes. A possible deviation (requiring CISO and VP approval) would be a right to terminate without fee if Meridian reasonably objects and Cloudvance proceeds anyway."),

dict(id="S-2", title="Flow-down obligations and Stratos visibility", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §8.2: subcontract terms must be **at least as protective** as the vendor agreement, covering (a) security, privacy and HIPAA/HITECH, including a **subcontractor BAA**; (b) the **same service levels**; (c) **audit rights for Meridian**; (d) data handling, portability and destruction; and (e) confidentiality. The vendor is fully liable for subcontractors, must make subcontracts available on request and must notify Meridian of subcontractor breaches.",
 agr="§7.2: Cloudvance is responsible and liable for Subcontractors and will enter into agreements \"**sufficient to enable Cloudvance to comply** with its obligations.\" §D.3(d): PHI subcontractors agree in writing to \"the same restrictions, conditions, and requirements\" as the BAA.",
 gap="The liability language in §7.2 and the PHI flow-down in §D.3(d) meet part of the SLS. The \"sufficient to enable\" standard is weaker than \"at least as protective.\" There is also no flow-down of service levels, Meridian audit rights or destruction obligations, and no right to review the Stratos agreement. The value of §7.2 is reduced by §15.1, which treats hosting failures as force majeure (A-6), and by §C.7, which extends resolution times when resolution depends on third-party vendors.",
 redline="Amend the last sentence of §7.2: \"Cloudvance shall bind each Subcontractor by written agreement to obligations **at least as protective of Customer** as those in this Agreement, including a subcontractor business associate agreement compliant with HIPAA/HITECH, service level commitments sufficient to support Exhibit C, audit rights exercisable by Cloudvance and Customer, and the data handling, portability, destruction and confidentiality obligations of this Agreement. Cloudvance shall make such agreements available to Customer on request and shall promptly notify Customer of any Subcontractor breach or non-compliance affecting Customer Data. Failures of Subcontractors shall not excuse Cloudvance\x27s performance.\"",
 position="Must-have. As part of diligence, request the Stratos SOC 2 and HITRUST reports, the Cloudvance–Stratos BAA and the data center list now."),

dict(id="S-3", title="Hosting location: any Stratos U.S. data center, movable at Cloudvance\x27s discretion", risk="Medium",
 sls="SLS §8.3: data may be hosted only in locations **approved in writing and listed by city and state** in a schedule. Data may not be moved or replicated to an unlisted site without **90 days\x27 notice and consent**, which Meridian may withhold in its sole discretion. Data must remain in the **continental United States** and may not be hosted, processed, stored **or accessed** from outside it without consent.",
 agr="§7.3: data may be hosted in \"any Stratos Cloud Services data center located in the United States.\" Cloudvance may move data between Stratos U.S. data centers \"at its discretion.\" Transfer or storage outside the U.S. requires consent. §E.6: backups are kept in geographically separate Stratos U.S. locations.",
 gap="There is no schedule of approved sites, no notice or consent for moves, and no restriction on **remote access** from outside the U.S. (for example, by offshore support personnel). \"United States\" could include non-continental states and territories. Moving data within Stratos also changes the subcontractor risk profile without Meridian\x27s knowledge.",
 redline="Replace §7.3: \"Customer Data (including backups) shall be hosted, processed and stored only at the data center locations listed by city and state in **Schedule 7.3**, each approved in writing by Customer. Cloudvance shall not migrate, replicate or transfer Customer Data to any other location without at least ninety (90) days\x27 prior written notice and Customer\x27s prior written consent, which Customer may withhold in its sole discretion. Customer Data shall at all times remain within the continental United States and shall not be hosted, processed, stored or **accessed** from any location outside the continental United States without Customer\x27s prior written consent.\"",
 position="Must-have for the offshore-access restriction and the schedule of sites. On moves between listed Stratos sites, a 30-day notice period could be considered as a fallback, which would be a deviation."),
]

input.command:
S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/intellectual-property/compare-saas-agreement-against-service-level-standards/claude-code-session/20261016-031537; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/build/gaps5.py <<'"'"'EOF'"'"'
GAPS_E = [
dict(id="F-1", title="Liability cap: 12 months of subscription fees ($6.84M) versus 24 months of total fees ($15.48M)", risk="Critical",
 sls="SLS §9.1: the cap must be at least **24 months of total fees**, including subscription, implementation and professional services fees. Using the SLS\x27s own worked example for this deal: ($6.84M + $4.5M / 5) × 2 = **$15.48M**. A cap based only on subscription fees must be flagged, with CISO, VP and General Counsel approval.",
 agr="§10.2: each party\x27s aggregate liability is capped at \"TWELVE (12) MONTHS OF SUBSCRIPTION FEES ... (I.E., ... $6,840,000.00).\" The only exception is §9 indemnification obligations. §10.3 applies the cap expressly to the BAA, Exhibit E data security and Exhibit C.",
 gap="The cap is **$8.64M (about 56%) below** the SLS minimum. It fails the SLS on both the multiplier (12 months instead of 24) and the base (subscription fees only, excluding the $4.5M implementation fee). It is also a single aggregate cap for the full five-year, $38.7M term (about 17.7% of contract value), so one significant breach could exhaust it for the rest of the relationship.",
 redline="Replace §10.2: \"Except for the Excluded Claims (Section 10.4), each Party\x27s total aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed an amount equal to **twenty-four (24) months of Total Fees**, where \"Total Fees\" means the annual Subscription Fee plus the Implementation Fees divided by the number of years in the initial Subscription Term (i.e., not less than **$15,480,000**).\" Consider also: the cap resets annually or is the greater of the fixed amount and fees paid in the preceding 24 months; and a separate, higher \"super-cap\" for data breach and BAA claims, with insurance limits matched to it (our recommendation).",
 position="Must-have at the $15.48M floor. A super-cap for data and privacy claims is the market approach for EHR deals and may be the realistic compromise if Cloudvance refuses an unlimited data breach carve-out. Any super-cap, however, must sit within the SLS §9.2 framework (see F-2)."),

dict(id="F-2", title="Consequential-damages exclusion expressly covers data breaches and the BAA; no carve-outs", risk="Critical",
 sls="SLS §9.2: a mutual exclusion is allowed, but the following must be **carved out** and subject at least to the full cap: (a) data breaches, including notification, credit monitoring, forensics, regulatory defense and penalties; (b) BAA violations; (c) third-party IP infringement; (d) willful misconduct or gross negligence, with **unlimited** liability; and (e) breach of confidentiality. An unqualified exclusion \"shall be returned to the vendor.\"",
 agr="§10.1 excludes indirect, consequential and similar damages, \"INCLUDING ... LOSS OF DATA ... BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE SERVICES,\" and adds that it applies to \"CLAIMS RELATED TO DATA SECURITY, DATA BREACHES, AND THE BAA.\" No carve-out exists for gross negligence, willful misconduct or confidentiality.",
 gap=["This is the reverse of SLS §9.2: the Agreement singles out exactly the claims the SLS requires to be carved out and confirms that they are subject to the exclusion. Cloudvance could argue that breach notification costs, credit monitoring, regulatory penalties, forensic costs and patient-care disruption costs are \"consequential\" and therefore not recoverable at all. If so, Meridian\x27s recovery for a major PHI breach could be close to zero, even within the $6.84M cap.",
  "Gross negligence and willful misconduct remain capped, and possibly excluded. Under the SLS they must be **unlimited**."],
 redline="Insert new §10.4 (Excluded Claims): \"The exclusions in Section 10.1 shall not apply to, and the following shall be recoverable as direct damages: (a) **Data Breach Costs**, meaning all costs of investigation, forensic analysis, notification, call centers, credit and identity monitoring, regulatory defense, fines, penalties and assessments arising from any unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure or loss of Customer Data or PHI caused by Cloudvance or its Subcontractors; (b) damages arising from breach of the BAA; (c) damages arising from infringement or misappropriation of third-party Intellectual Property Rights; and (d) damages arising from breach of Section 5 (Confidentiality). Claims under (a) to (d) shall be subject to the cap in Section 10.2. **Liability arising from a Party\x27s gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud shall not be subject to any exclusion or limitation of liability.**\" Delete the last sentence of §10.1, and delete the references to the BAA, Exhibit E and Exhibit C in §10.3.",
 position="Must-have and, under SLS §9.2, a gating issue on the same footing as the sole-remedy clause."),

dict(id="F-3", title="Indemnification: narrow vendor indemnity, broad and uncapped customer indemnity", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §9.2(a) to (c) and §10.5 assume vendor responsibility for data breach, BAA and IP claims, and §10.5 requires indemnification obligations to survive. Marcus Ellison specifically asked for liability and indemnification to be covered.",
 agr="§9.1: Cloudvance indemnifies only against claims that use of the Platform infringes a **U.S.** patent, copyright or trademark. Trade secrets and non-U.S. rights are not covered, and the indemnity has broad combination exclusions. §8.2(d): the non-infringement warranty is qualified \"to Cloudvance\x27s knowledge.\" §9.2: **Meridian** indemnifies Cloudvance for all claims \"arising out of or relating to ... Customer Data,\" a standard that is not fault-based except where Cloudvance\x27s breach caused the claim. Because §10.2 excludes §9 from the cap, Meridian\x27s indemnity is **uncapped**.",
 gap="Cloudvance gives no indemnity for third-party and regulatory claims arising from its own data breaches, BAA violations, violations of law, or bodily injury and property damage. Those are the claims most likely to arise for an EHR vendor, for example patient class actions after a breach. In contrast, Meridian\x27s indemnity for anything \"relating to Customer Data\" could be read to require Meridian to defend Cloudvance against patient claims arising from a breach at Cloudvance, unless Meridian proves Cloudvance breached the Agreement. The imbalance is significant.",
 redline="Expand §9.1 to add: \"(b) any breach of the BAA or Exhibit E, or any Security Incident or Breach involving Customer Data caused by Cloudvance or its Subcontractors; (c) Cloudvance\x27s violation of applicable law, including HIPAA/HITECH; (d) gross negligence or willful misconduct of Cloudvance or its Subcontractors; and (e) bodily injury, death or property damage caused by Cloudvance.\" Extend IP coverage to infringement or misappropriation of any Intellectual Property Rights, worldwide, and delete the knowledge qualifier in §8.2(d). Narrow §9.2(a) to claims that Customer Data, as provided by Customer, infringes third-party IP rights or was provided in violation of law. Make Meridian\x27s indemnity subject to the §10.2 cap.",
 position="Must-have for the data breach and BAA indemnity and for narrowing the customer indemnity. The worldwide IP scope is a should-have, because Meridian operates only in the U.S."),

dict(id="G-1", title="Termination for cause: 60-day cure period; no definition of material breach", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §10.1: Meridian may terminate for material breach not cured within **30 days**. Material breach includes failing uptime commitments for **2 consecutive months**, security or BAA failures, unauthorized use or disclosure of Customer Data, failure to provide transition assistance, and violation of law. No termination fee applies, and data retrieval and transition rights continue.",
 agr="§11.2: either party may terminate on **60 days\x27** notice if a material breach is not cured within that period. Material breach is not defined. §D.6: BAA breaches route to §11.2.",
 gap="The cure period is twice the SLS standard. Because material breach is undefined, Meridian would face arguments over whether SLA misses (which the Agreement makes non-binding) or security failures count. A mutual 60-day cure also benefits Cloudvance if Meridian is in a payment dispute.",
 redline="Amend §11.2: \"Customer may terminate this Agreement upon written notice if Cloudvance commits a material breach and fails to cure it within **thirty (30) days** after written notice. Material breach by Cloudvance includes: (a) failure to meet the Monthly Uptime commitment in any two (2) consecutive months; (b) failure to comply with Exhibit E or the BAA; (c) any unauthorized use or disclosure of Customer Data; (d) failure to provide transition assistance; and (e) failure to comply with applicable law.\" Confirm that no termination fee applies and that §§6.5 and 11.7 continue to apply.",
 position="Must-have."),

dict(id="G-2", title="Termination for convenience: 180 days\x27 notice and termination fee", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §10.2: **90 days\x27** notice, with **no termination fee, penalty or remaining-term fee**. Pre-paid fees for services not yet rendered are refunded pro rata.",
 agr="§11.3: **180 days\x27** notice plus a termination fee equal to the unpaid quarterly installments for the current contract year, stated to be liquidated damages and \"not a penalty.\" §4.1: fees are \"non-cancellable and non-refundable.\" §11.5(b) makes the termination fee payable on termination.",
 gap="Depending on timing, the fee could reach $5.13M (three quarterly installments) if termination takes effect just after a July 1 payment. That is on top of roughly two quarters of fees ($3.42M) paid during the 180-day notice period. Prepaid fees are not refunded. The structure makes a convenience exit far more expensive than the SLS allows.",
 redline="Amend §11.3: \"Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon **ninety (90) days\x27** prior written notice. **No termination fee, early termination penalty or remaining-term fee shall apply.** Cloudvance shall refund, within thirty (30) days, any prepaid fees attributable to the period after the effective date of termination.\" Conform §4.1 (\"except as expressly set forth in this Agreement, including Sections 11.3 and C.4\") and §11.5(b).",
 position="Must-have under the SLS. Expect significant resistance, because Cloudvance\x27s implementation pricing likely assumes five years of subscription revenue. If Meridian\x27s leadership considers a compromise, one option would be a declining fee in years 1 and 2 only, set at no more than unamortized implementation cost. That would be an SLS deviation requiring approval."),

dict(id="G-3", title="No termination right for data breach; \"no other termination rights\" clause", risk="Critical",
 sls="SLS §10.4: immediate termination on notice for a data breach or security incident affecting PHI or Customer Data. The vendor gets a **10-day cure** only if it (a) shows full containment, (b) completes all HIPAA, HITECH and state notifications, and (c) delivers a satisfactory remediation plan. Otherwise termination takes effect automatically. No fee applies. SLS §10.3: chronic SLA failure termination (see B-4).",
 agr="No breach-specific termination right. §11.4: \"No other termination rights, whether arising by operation of law or otherwise.\" §D.6 routes BAA breaches through the 60-day §11.2 process. §15.1 separately allows termination after 90 days of force majeure, which is internally inconsistent with §11.4.",
 gap="After a ransomware attack or significant PHI breach, Meridian would have to give 60 days\x27 notice, and Cloudvance could defeat termination by \"curing.\" §11.4 could also be argued to waive common-law remedies for repudiation or fundamental breach. HIPAA (45 CFR §164.504(e)(2)(iii)) requires that a BAA authorize termination by the covered entity for a material violation. The §D.6 cross-reference likely satisfies that requirement, but the 60-day cure period is far longer than the SLS allows.",
 redline="Insert new §11.8 (Termination for Data Breach), reproducing SLS §10.4 in full, including the 10-day conditional cure and automatic termination. Replace §11.4: \"The termination rights in this Agreement are cumulative and in addition to any other rights and remedies available at law or in equity.\" Amend §D.6 to cross-reference §11.8.",
 position="Must-have."),

dict(id="G-4", title="Effect of termination and survival", risk="Medium",
 sls="SLS §10.5: data ownership, retrieval, transition, liability limits, confidentiality, indemnification, **insurance** and **accrued service credits** survive. SLS §4.2: credits are paid in cash after termination.",
 agr="§11.5(e): survival includes §§5, 6.1, **6.3 and 6.4 (Cloudvance\x27s data rights)**, 6.5, 9, 10, 12 and 14. There is no transition provision and no survival of credits, which are forfeited under §C.4. §5.1: confidentiality survives only **3 years** from disclosure, except for trade secrets.",
 gap="The survival clause preserves Cloudvance\x27s data rights while Meridian\x27s accrued credits are forfeited. A three-year confidentiality tail is inadequate for PHI and patient records, which require protection for as long as Cloudvance or its Subcontractors hold them.",
 redline="Amend §11.5(e): delete §§6.3 and 6.4, and add accrued Service Credits, §11.7 (Transition Assistance), §12 (Insurance) and the BAA. Amend §5.1: \"provided that obligations with respect to Customer Data and PHI shall survive for so long as Cloudvance or any Subcontractor retains such data.\"",
 position="Must-have, as a conforming change to the other items in this memo."),

dict(id="H-1", title="Audit rights: once per year, BAA-only scope, and SOC 2 can replace the audit", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §11.1: **at least 2 audits per calendar year** on 30 days\x27 notice, plus **for-cause audits** on shorter notice (after an incident, a subcontractor or location change, or a regulatory inquiry). SLS §11.2: scope covers security, BAA, SLA performance, data handling and subcontractors, including **physical inspection of data centers**, interviews, log review, **subcontractor audits** and DR testing. The vendor \"**shall not satisfy** its audit obligations solely by providing a SOC 2 Type II report.\" SLS §11.3: Meridian pays for routine audits, but the vendor **reimburses audit costs and funds remediation** if there is material non-compliance.",
 agr="§13.1: no more than **once per year**, on **60 days\x27** notice, limited to **BAA compliance**, at Customer\x27s sole expense, using an auditor \"reasonably acceptable to Cloudvance,\" during business hours. Meridian must deliver a summary of findings to Cloudvance. §13.2: Cloudvance may, \"at its sole discretion,\" satisfy **any** audit request with its SOC 2 Type II report, which \"shall be deemed to satisfy any and all audit requests\" for the year and eliminates on-site rights.",
 gap="In practice, §13.2 means Meridian has no audit right: Cloudvance can respond to every request by sending its SOC 2 report, which SLS §11.2 specifically prohibits. Even without §13.2, the scope excludes SLA performance, security outside the BAA, data handling and Stratos. There is no for-cause audit, no physical inspection and no cost-shifting for non-compliance.",
 redline="Replace §13 with the SLS §11 framework: two scheduled audits per calendar year on thirty (30) days\x27 notice; for-cause audits on reasonable notice following a Security Incident, suspected non-compliance, a change in Subcontractors or hosting locations, or a regulatory inquiry; the full SLS §11.2(a) to (g) scope, including physical inspection of data centers and audits of Subcontractors (including Stratos), directly or through Cloudvance; delete §13.2 and state that \"**SOC 2 Type II or other third-party reports may supplement but shall not replace Customer\x27s audit rights**\"; and if material non-compliance is found, Cloudvance reimburses all audit costs and bears all remediation costs. Delete the \"reasonably acceptable to Cloudvance\" approval right, or limit it to auditors that are Cloudvance competitors.",
 position="Must-have for deleting §13.2, expanding the scope, and adding for-cause audits. The second annual audit and the cost-shifting provision are also SLS requirements. If Cloudvance resists, a single comprehensive annual audit plus unlimited for-cause audits would be a deviation requiring approval."),

dict(id="I-1", title="Governing law: Texas versus North Carolina", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §12.1: agreements must be governed by **North Carolina** law. Any other choice requires prior written approval from Meridian\x27s General Counsel.",
 agr="§14.1: Texas law, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.",
 gap="Marcus Ellison expected that this would not be acceptable, and the SLS confirms it. Meridian is a North Carolina corporation, headquartered in Charlotte, with facilities in NC, SC and GA. Texas law would apply to questions such as the enforceability of the liquidated-damages termination fee (§11.3), the limitation-of-liability provisions and the jury waiver.",
 redline="Replace §14.1: \"This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of North Carolina, without giving effect to any choice-of-law or conflict-of-law rules that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.\"",
 position="Must-have without General Counsel approval. Delaware law (Cloudvance\x27s state of incorporation) is sometimes offered as a \"neutral\" compromise, but it would still require General Counsel approval."),

dict(id="I-2", title="Mandatory AAA arbitration in Austin; jury waiver embedded in the form", risk="High",
 sls="SLS §12.2: **litigation in state or federal courts in Mecklenburg County, NC**, with exclusive jurisdiction. Optional **non-binding** mediation in Charlotte may be included, but it cannot be a prerequisite to suit. SLS §12.3: **no mandatory binding arbitration for disputes over $1,000,000**. Arbitration of disputes of $1M or less is allowed only if seated in Charlotte, under NC law, with an arbitrator who has healthcare IT or regulatory expertise. Jury waivers are allowed only in a **separately executed** document.",
 agr="§14.2: **all** disputes, including arbitrability, go to binding AAA Commercial arbitration before a single arbitrator seated in **Austin, Texas**. The arbitrator\x27s authority is subject to the §10 limitations. Proceedings are confidential, and each party bears its own fees. §14.3: an all-caps jury waiver in the body of the Agreement.",
 gap="Any significant dispute under a $38.7M contract will exceed the $1M threshold, so under SLS §12.3 mandatory arbitration is presumptively impermissible here. A single arbitrator in Austin, with limited discovery, no appeal and confidential proceedings, combined with Texas law and the §10 limitations, would give Cloudvance substantial procedural leverage. The jury waiver fails the SLS requirement for a separately executed document. There is also no carve-out allowing either party to seek injunctive relief, for example to compel data return or continued service, which an EHR customer may urgently need.",
 redline="Replace §14.2: \"Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, and each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive personal jurisdiction and venue of such courts and waives any objection based on inconvenient forum. The Parties may, by mutual agreement, submit a dispute to non-binding mediation in Charlotte, North Carolina, but mediation shall not be a prerequisite to filing suit.\" Optionally add: disputes of $1,000,000 or less may be arbitrated in Charlotte under NC law before an arbitrator with healthcare IT or regulatory expertise. Delete §14.3; any jury waiver must be a separately executed instrument. Add: \"Nothing herein limits either Party\x27s right to seek injunctive or other equitable relief, including to compel the return of Customer Data or the continuation of Services.\"",
 position="Must-have. If Cloudvance insists on arbitration, the SLS allows it only for disputes of $1M or less and only in Charlotte."),
]

S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/intellectual-property/compare-saas-agreement-against-service-level-standards/claude-code-session/20261016-031537; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/build/main.py <<'"'"'EOF'"'"'
import math, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/build")
from lib import *
from gaps1 import GAPS_A
from gaps2 import GAPS_B
from gaps3 import GAPS_C
from gaps4 import GAPS_D
from gaps5 import GAPS_E
from docx.enum.text import WD_BREAK

ALL = GAPS_A + GAPS_B + GAPS_C + GAPS_D + GAPS_E
d = new_doc()

# header / footer
sec = d.sections[0]
hp = sec.header.paragraphs[0]; hp.text = "PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL | ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION | ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT"
hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
for r in hp.runs: r.font.size = Pt(8); r.bold = True
fp = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]; fp.text = "Cloudvance ClinicalEdge MSA: Gap Analysis Against Meridian SLS v4.2 | Draft for client review"
fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
for r in fp.runs: r.font.size = Pt(8)

t = d.add_paragraph(); t.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
r = t.add_run("MEMORANDUM"); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(16)

hdr = [("TO:", "Marcus Ellison, Vice President, IT Procurement, Meridian Health Systems, Inc."),
       ("CC:", "Dr. Priya Nandakumar, Chief Information Security Officer, Meridian Health Systems, Inc."),
       ("FROM:", "Sarah Langford, Whitfield Crane"),
       ("DATE:", "November 24, 2025"),
       ("RE:", "Gap Analysis: Cloudvance Technologies, Inc. Master SaaS Agreement (ClinicalEdge™ Platform, dated November 4, 2025, Exhibits A to E) Compared with Meridian Service Level Standards for IT Procurement, Version 4.2 (October 15, 2025)")]
ht = d.add_table(rows=0, cols=2)
for k, v in hdr:
    c = ht.add_row().cells
    c[0].text = ""; rr = c[0].paragraphs[0].add_run(k); rr.bold = True
    c[1].text = ""; c[1].paragraphs[0].add_run(v)
    c[0].width = Inches(0.9); c[1].width = Inches(5.6)
p = d.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr(); bdr = OxmlElement("w:pBdr"); b = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
b.set(qn("w:val"), "single"); b.set(qn("w:sz"), "8"); b.set(qn("w:space"), "1"); b.set(qn("w:color"), "1F3A5F"); bdr.append(b); pPr.append(bdr)

# ---------- I. Executive summary
d.add_heading("I. Executive Summary", level=1)
para(d, "You asked for a comprehensive gap analysis comparing the proposed Cloudvance Master SaaS Agreement (the \"**Agreement**\"), including Exhibits A to E, with Meridian\x27s Service Level Standards v4.2 (the \"**SLS**\"). The Agreement covers the ClinicalEdge EHR, clinical decision support, patient portal and revenue cycle management modules for a total contract value of $38.7 million over five years.")
para(d, "**Bottom line: the Agreement should not be executed in its current form.** It is a vendor-favorable form that falls below the SLS in every area you asked us to review. We identified **%d material deviations**, of which **%d are rated Critical** and **%d High**. Many of these involve specific language the SLS says must be rejected. Under SLS §1.1, any deviation that remains at signing requires written approval from both the CISO and the VP of IT Procurement, documented on the deviation approval form. Some deviations also require General Counsel approval (SLS §9.1 for the liability cap and §12.1 for governing law)." % (len(ALL), sum(g["risk"]=="Critical" for g in ALL), sum(g["risk"]=="High" for g in ALL)))
para(d, "**Three provisions trigger the SLS \"return to vendor\" rule.** The SLS directs that a draft containing any of the following be returned to the vendor for revision. We recommend that the first redline be sent to Cloudvance with these three items identified as preconditions to substantive negotiation:")
bullet(d, "**Ex. C §C.5:** service credits are the \"sole and exclusive remedy\" for uptime failures (SLS §4.3).")
bullet(d, "**Ex. C §C.7 and Ex. A §A.3(c):** incident response and resolution times are \"commercially reasonable targets\" that \"do not constitute binding commitments\" (SLS §5.4).")
bullet(d, "**§10.1:** an unqualified consequential-damages exclusion that applies expressly to \"data security, data breaches, and the BAA\" (SLS §9.2).")
para(d, "**Answers to the specific questions in your November 10 email:**")
bullet(d, "**Uptime and maintenance.** You are right to be concerned. The 99.5% figure is the SLS **Tier 3** standard, and it is only a \"commercially reasonable efforts\" covenant. Tier 1 requires a guaranteed 99.95%. The maintenance terms make the gap much worse: up to 8 hours per week of excluded Scheduled Maintenance (versus 4 hours per month), 24 hours\x27 notice (versus 72), and a blanket exclusion of Emergency Maintenance, which Cloudvance alone defines. On a worst-case reading, the Platform could be unavailable about 6% of a month (effective availability of roughly 94%) and still be reported as meeting the SLA (A-2 to A-5).")
bullet(d, "**Do the service credits have real teeth?** No. Credits begin only below 99.5%, top out at 15% of the monthly fee ($85,500), and are capped at about $1.03M per year (roughly 2.7% of contract value). They are lost if Meridian does not claim them within 30 days, cannot be paid in cash, are forfeited on termination, and are the sole and exclusive remedy. The Agreement contains no chronic-failure termination right, and §11.4 rules one out (B-1 to B-4).")
bullet(d, "**Exit and data.** Retrieval is limited to 30 days (versus 90), in a \"commercially standard format\" (versus HL7 FHIR and CSV), with Meridian \"solely responsible\" for retrieval and Cloudvance free to delete afterward in its sole discretion. The Agreement has **no transition assistance at all** (E-3, E-4). A convenience exit costs 180 days\x27 notice plus a fee of up to $5.13M (G-2).")
bullet(d, "**Data license.** It is broader than the SLS allows in every respect. It is a worldwide license to modify and create derivative works from identifiable Customer Data in order to \"improve\" Cloudvance\x27s services, with unrestricted rights to de-identified data, Cloudvance ownership of \"Aggregated Data\" for \"any lawful business purpose,\" and survival of all of these rights after termination (E-1, E-2).")
bullet(d, "**BAA and HIPAA/HITECH.** Dr. Nandakumar\x27s concern is confirmed. Exhibit D references only HIPAA and 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164. It does not mention the HITECH Act (42 U.S.C. §17931 et seq.) or the Omnibus Rule, and so fails SLS §6.1 on its face. The BAA also sets a 30-day breach notice period, sets no deadline for reporting Security Incidents, and authorizes Cloudvance\x27s de-identified data program (D-1, D-2).")
bullet(d, "**Security certifications.** The Agreement requires only SOC 2 Type II, with no scope or currency requirements. HITRUST CSF, annual penetration testing and quarterly vulnerability scanning are all absent. Encryption is described only as \"industry-standard,\" language the SLS expressly prohibits (D-3, D-4).")
bullet(d, "**Stratos and subcontractors.** Cloudvance may add subcontractors without consent and need only give notice within 30 days afterward. Flow-down obligations are weak. Most significantly, the force majeure clause (§15.1) treats \"failure of third-party hosting or cloud infrastructure services\" as force majeure, so a Stratos outage would excuse Cloudvance and would not count against uptime. Hosting may be at any Stratos U.S. site, and there is no restriction on offshore access (A-6, S-1 to S-3).")
bullet(d, "**Liability and indemnity.** The cap is 12 months of subscription fees ($6.84M), compared with the SLS minimum of 24 months of total fees ($15.48M), a shortfall of $8.64M. None of the required carve-outs is present, so gross negligence is capped. The vendor indemnity covers only U.S. IP infringement, while Meridian gives a broad indemnity for anything \"relating to Customer Data\" that is **uncapped** (F-1 to F-3).")
bullet(d, "**Insurance.** As you suspected, the Agreement is effectively silent. §12 requires only \"commercially reasonable insurance,\" compared with the SLS minimum of $10M in cyber and technology E&O coverage, additional-insured status, certificates of insurance and cancellation notice (D-6).")
bullet(d, "**Audit, governing law and disputes.** The Agreement allows one BAA-only audit per year, which Cloudvance can satisfy by sending its SOC 2 report. It selects Texas law and mandatory AAA arbitration in Austin, with a jury waiver embedded in the form. Each of these contravenes SLS §§11 and 12 (H-1, I-1, I-2).")
para(d, "**Timeline note.** LegacyMed expires on **March 31, 2026**, but the target ClinicalEdge Go-Live is **July 1, 2026**, and Cloudvance commits only to \"commercially reasonable efforts\" to meet it (§3.3). The Agreement does not address the three-month gap, and Cloudvance bears no consequence for delay. Unless a LegacyMed extension or bridge is already secured, this is an operational risk that sits alongside the SLS issues, and it affects Meridian\x27s negotiating leverage: Cloudvance may assume that Meridian has to sign quickly. See Part V.")

# ---------- II. Scope

    inc = math.ceil(round(sf / 0.1, 6))

    return 15

# ---------- I. Executive summary
d.add_heading("I. Executive Summary", level=1)
para(d, "You asked for a comprehensive gap analysis comparing the proposed Cloudvance Master SaaS Agreement (the \"**Agreement**\"), including Exhibits A to E, with Meridian\x27s Service Level Standards v4.2 (the \"**SLS**\"). The Agreement covers the ClinicalEdge EHR, clinical decision support, patient portal and revenue cycle management modules for a total contract value of $38.7 million over five years.")
para(d, "**Bottom line: the Agreement should not be executed in its current form.** It is a vendor-favorable form that falls below the SLS in every area you asked us to review. We identified **%d material deviations**, of which **%d are rated Critical** and **%d High**. Many of these involve specific language the SLS says must be rejected. Under SLS §1.1, any deviation that remains at signing requires written approval from both the CISO and the VP of IT Procurement, documented on the deviation approval form. Some deviations also require General Counsel approval (SLS §9.1 for the liability cap and §12.1 for governing law)." % (len(ALL), sum(g["risk"]=="Critical" for g in ALL), sum(g["risk"]=="High" for g in ALL)))
para(d, "**Three provisions trigger the SLS \"return to vendor\" rule.** The SLS directs that a draft containing any of the following be returned to the vendor for revision. We recommend that the first redline be sent to Cloudvance with these three items identified as preconditions to substantive negotiation:")
bullet(d, "**Ex. C §C.5:** service credits are the \"sole and exclusive remedy\" for uptime failures (SLS §4.3).")
bullet(d, "**Ex. C §C.7 and Ex. A §A.3(c):** incident response and resolution times are \"commercially reasonable targets\" that \"do not constitute binding commitments\" (SLS §5.4).")
bullet(d, "**§10.1:** an unqualified consequential-damages exclusion that applies expressly to \"data security, data breaches, and the BAA\" (SLS §9.2).")
para(d, "**Answers to the specific questions in your November 10 email:**")
bullet(d, "**Uptime and maintenance.** You are right to be concerned. The 99.5% figure is the SLS **Tier 3** standard, and it is only a \"commercially reasonable efforts\" covenant. Tier 1 requires a guaranteed 99.95%. The maintenance terms make the gap much worse: up to 8 hours per week of excluded Scheduled Maintenance (versus 4 hours per month), 24 hours\x27 notice (versus 72), and a blanket exclusion of Emergency Maintenance, which Cloudvance alone defines. On a worst-case reading, the Platform could be unavailable about 6% of a month (effective availability of roughly 94%) and still be reported as meeting the SLA (A-2 to A-5).")
bullet(d, "**Do the service credits have real teeth?** No. Credits begin only below 99.5%, top out at 15% of the monthly fee ($85,500), and are capped at about $1.03M per year (roughly 2.7% of contract value). They are lost if Meridian does not claim them within 30 days, cannot be paid in cash, are forfeited on termination, and are the sole and exclusive remedy. The Agreement contains no chronic-failure termination right, and §11.4 rules one out (B-1 to B-4).")
bullet(d, "**Exit and data.** Retrieval is limited to 30 days (versus 90), in a \"commercially standard format\" (versus HL7 FHIR and CSV), with Meridian \"solely responsible\" for retrieval and Cloudvance free to delete afterward in its sole discretion. The Agreement has **no transition assistance at all** (E-3, E-4). A convenience exit costs 180 days\x27 notice plus a fee of up to $5.13M (G-2).")
bullet(d, "**Data license.** It is broader than the SLS allows in every respect. It is a worldwide license to modify and create derivative works from identifiable Customer Data in order to \"improve\" Cloudvance\x27s services, with unrestricted rights to de-identified data, Cloudvance ownership of \"Aggregated Data\" for \"any lawful business purpose,\" and survival of all of these rights after termination (E-1, E-2).")
bullet(d, "**BAA and HIPAA/HITECH.** Dr. Nandakumar\x27s concern is confirmed. Exhibit D references only HIPAA and 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164. It does not mention the HITECH Act (42 U.S.C. §17931 et seq.) or the Omnibus Rule, and so fails SLS §6.1 on its face. The BAA also sets a 30-day breach notice period, sets no deadline for reporting Security Incidents, and authorizes Cloudvance\x27s de-identified data program (D-1, D-2).")
bullet(d, "**Security certifications.** The Agreement requires only SOC 2 Type II, with no scope or currency requirements. HITRUST CSF, annual penetration testing and quarterly vulnerability scanning are all absent. Encryption is described only as \"industry-standard,\" language the SLS expressly prohibits (D-3, D-4).")
bullet(d, "**Stratos and subcontractors.** Cloudvance may add subcontractors without consent and need only give notice within 30 days afterward. Flow-down obligations are weak. Most significantly, the force majeure clause (§15.1) treats \"failure of third-party hosting or cloud infrastructure services\" as force majeure, so a Stratos outage would excuse Cloudvance and would not count against uptime. Hosting may be at any Stratos U.S. site, and there is no restriction on offshore access (A-6, S-1 to S-3).")
bullet(d, "**Liability and indemnity.** The cap is 12 months of subscription fees ($6.84M), compared with the SLS minimum of 24 months of total fees ($15.48M), a shortfall of $8.64M. None of the required carve-outs is present, so gross negligence is capped. The vendor indemnity covers only U.S. IP infringement, while Meridian gives a broad indemnity for anything \"relating to Customer Data\" that is **uncapped** (F-1 to F-3).")
bullet(d, "**Insurance.** As you suspected, the Agreement is effectively silent. §12 requires only \"commercially reasonable insurance,\" compared with the SLS minimum of $10M in cyber and technology E&O coverage, additional-insured status, certificates of insurance and cancellation notice (D-6).")
bullet(d, "**Audit, governing law and disputes.** The Agreement allows one BAA-only audit per year, which Cloudvance can satisfy by sending its SOC 2 report. It selects Texas law and mandatory AAA arbitration in Austin, with a jury waiver embedded in the form. Each of these contravenes SLS §§11 and 12 (H-1, I-1, I-2).")
para(d, "**Timeline note.** LegacyMed expires on **March 31, 2026**, but the target ClinicalEdge Go-Live is **July 1, 2026**, and Cloudvance commits only to \"commercially reasonable efforts\" to meet it (§3.3). The Agreement does not address the three-month gap, and Cloudvance bears no consequence for delay. Unless a LegacyMed extension or bridge is already secured, this is an operational risk that sits alongside the SLS issues, and it affects Meridian\x27s negotiating leverage: Cloudvance may assume that Meridian has to sign quickly. See Part V.")

**MEMORANDUM**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **TO:**                             Marcus Ellison, Vice President, IT Procurement, Meridian Health Systems, Inc.
  ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **CC:**                             Dr. Priya Nandakumar, Chief Information Security Officer, Meridian Health Systems, Inc.

  **FROM:**                           Sarah Langford, Whitfield Crane

  **DATE:**                           November 24, 2025

  **RE:**                             Gap Analysis: Cloudvance Technologies, Inc. Master SaaS Agreement (ClinicalEdge™ Platform, dated November 4, 2025, Exhibits A to E) Compared with Meridian Service Level Standards for IT Procurement, Version 4.2 (October 15, 2025)
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# I. Executive Summary

You asked for a comprehensive gap analysis comparing the proposed Cloudvance Master SaaS Agreement (the \"**Agreement**\"), including Exhibits A to E, with Meridian\'s Service Level Standards v4.2 (the \"**SLS**\"). The Agreement covers the ClinicalEdge EHR, clinical decision support, patient portal and revenue cycle management modules for a total contract value of \$38.7 million over five years.

**Bottom line: the Agreement should not be executed in its current form.** It is a vendor-favorable form that falls below the SLS in every area you asked us to review. We identified **38 material deviations**, of which **14 are rated Critical** and **20 High**. Many of these involve specific language the SLS says must be rejected. Under SLS §1.1, any deviation that remains at signing requires written approval from both the CISO and the VP of IT Procurement, documented on the deviation approval form. Some deviations also require General Counsel approval (SLS §9.1 for the liability cap and §12.1 for governing law).

**Three provisions trigger the SLS \"return to vendor\" rule.** The SLS directs that a draft containing any of the following be returned to the vendor for revision. We recommend that the first redline be sent to Cloudvance with these three items identified as preconditions to substantive negotiation:

- **Ex. C §C.5:** service credits are the \"sole and exclusive remedy\" for uptime failures (SLS §4.3).

- **Ex. C §C.7 and Ex. A §A.3(c):** incident response and resolution times are \"commercially reasonable targets\" that \"do not constitute binding commitments\" (SLS §5.4).

- **§10.1:** an unqualified consequential-damages exclusion that applies expressly to \"data security, data breaches, and the BAA\" (SLS §9.2).

**Answers to the specific questions in your November 10 email:**

- **Uptime and maintenance.** You are right to be concerned. The 99.5% figure is the SLS **Tier 3** standard, and it is only a \"commercially reasonable efforts\" covenant. Tier 1 requires a guaranteed 99.95%. The maintenance terms make the gap much worse: up to 8 hours per week of excluded Scheduled Maintenance (versus 4 hours per month), 24 hours\' notice (versus 72), and a blanket exclusion of Emergency Maintenance, which Cloudvance alone defines. On a worst-case reading, the Platform could be unavailable about 6% of a month (effective availability of roughly 94%) and still be reported as meeting the SLA (A-2 to A-5).

- **Do the service credits have real teeth?** No. Credits begin only below 99.5%, top out at 15% of the monthly fee (\$85,500), and are capped at about \$1.03M per year (roughly 2.7% of contract value). They are lost if Meridian does not claim them within 30 days, cannot be paid in cash, are forfeited on termination, and are the sole and exclusive remedy. The Agreement contains no chronic-failure termination right, and §11.4 rules one out (B-1 to B-4).

- **Exit and data.** Retrieval is limited to 30 days (versus 90), in a \"commercially standard format\" (versus HL7 FHIR and CSV), with Meridian \"solely responsible\" for retrieval and Cloudvance free to delete afterward in its sole discretion. The Agreement has **no transition assistance at all** (E-3, E-4). A convenience exit costs 180 days\' notice plus a fee of up to \$5.13M (G-2).

- **Data license.** It is broader than the SLS allows in every respect. It is a worldwide license to modify and create derivative works from identifiable Customer Data in order to \"improve\" Cloudvance\'s services, with unrestricted rights to de-identified data, Cloudvance ownership of \"Aggregated Data\" for \"any lawful business purpose,\" and survival of all of these rights after termination (E-1, E-2).

- **BAA and HIPAA/HITECH.** Dr. Nandakumar\'s concern is confirmed. Exhibit D references only HIPAA and 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164. It does not mention the HITECH Act (42 U.S.C. §17931 et seq.) or the Omnibus Rule, and so fails SLS §6.1 on its face. The BAA also sets a 30-day breach notice period, sets no deadline for reporting Security Incidents, and authorizes Cloudvance\'s de-identified data program (D-1, D-2).

- **Security certifications.** The Agreement requires only SOC 2 Type II, with no scope or currency requirements. HITRUST CSF, annual penetration testing and quarterly vulnerability scanning are all absent. Encryption is described only as \"industry-standard,\" language the SLS expressly prohibits (D-3, D-4).

- **Stratos and subcontractors.** Cloudvance may add subcontractors without consent and need only give notice within 30 days afterward. Flow-down obligations are weak. Most significantly, the force majeure clause (§15.1) treats \"failure of third-party hosting or cloud infrastructure services\" as force majeure, so a Stratos outage would excuse Cloudvance and would not count against uptime. Hosting may be at any Stratos U.S. site, and there is no restriction on offshore access (A-6, S-1 to S-3).

- **Liability and indemnity.** The cap is 12 months of subscription fees (\$6.84M), compared with the SLS minimum of 24 months of total fees (\$15.48M), a shortfall of \$8.64M. None of the required carve-outs is present, so gross negligence is capped. The vendor indemnity covers only U.S. IP infringement, while Meridian gives a broad indemnity for anything \"relating to Customer Data\" that is **uncapped** (F-1 to F-3).

- **Insurance.** As you suspected, the Agreement is effectively silent. §12 requires only \"commercially reasonable insurance,\" compared with the SLS minimum of \$10M in cyber and technology E&O coverage, additional-insured status, certificates of insurance and cancellation notice (D-6).

- **Audit, governing law and disputes.** The Agreement allows one BAA-only audit per year, which Cloudvance can satisfy by sending its SOC 2 report. It selects Texas law and mandatory AAA arbitration in Austin, with a jury waiver embedded in the form. Each of these contravenes SLS §§11 and 12 (H-1, I-1, I-2).

**Timeline note.** LegacyMed expires on **March 31, 2026**, but the target ClinicalEdge Go-Live is **July 1, 2026**, and Cloudvance commits only to \"commercially reasonable efforts\" to meet it (§3.3). The Agreement does not address the three-month gap, and Cloudvance bears no consequence for delay. Unless a LegacyMed extension or bridge is already secured, this is an operational risk that sits alongside the SLS issues, and it affects Meridian\'s negotiating leverage: Cloudvance may assume that Meridian has to sign quickly. See Part V.

# II. Scope, Documents Reviewed and Methodology

**Documents reviewed.** (1) Cloudvance Master SaaS Agreement dated November 4, 2025, Sections 1 to 15 and Exhibits A (Scope of Services), B (Fees and Payment), C (Service Level Agreement), D (Business Associate Agreement) and E (Data Security). (2) Meridian Service Level Standards for Information Technology Procurement, v4.2, effective October 15, 2025, including Appendices A and B. (3) Your email of November 10, 2025, which sets out the business context and focus areas.

Under SLS §2.2.1 and §2.3, all four ClinicalEdge modules (EHR, CDS, patient portal and clinically integrated RCM) are Tier 1 \"without exception.\" We then compared each SLS requirement with the corresponding Agreement provision, and also flagged requirements on which the Agreement is silent.
